activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instruction, 25 mins planning and categorizing, 10 mins sharing.
activities.task: Create a shopping list for a local market, selecting plants and categorizing them into food, medicine, and raw materials.

activities.differentiation: Provide pre-cut images for students with fine motor difficulties.
activities.mastery_criterion: Poster accurately places at least two local crops into their correct utility categories.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instruction, 40 minutes creating posters, 10 minutes gallery walk.
activities.task: Create a poster classifying local crops into food, medicine, and raw materials.

activities.differentiation: Reduce the number of pairs for students who need a simplified task.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students successfully match all plant cards to their correct utility category.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes explaining rules, 25 minutes playing the game, 10 minutes review.
activities.task: Play a matching game where students pair a plant with the human need it satisfies (e.g., aloe for medicine, wood for building).

activities.differentiation: Provide explicit verbal cues for items that might be ambiguous.
activities.mastery_criterion: Items are correctly sorted into food, medicine, or raw materials based on their plant origin.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instruction, 25 minutes sorting, 10 minutes discussing results.
activities.safety: Ensure items are clean and safe to handle.
activities.task: Sort a mixed basket of everyday items (e.g., wooden spoon, herbal tea box, apple) into plant utility categories.

activities.differentiation: Allow oral sorting for students who struggle with reading the list.
activities.mastery_criterion: Passes if all provided plants are placed in a plausible utility category.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instructions, 25 minutes completing the assessment, 10 minutes collection.
activities.task: Sort a provided list of plants (e.g., corn, mint, cotton) into categories: food, medicine, and raw materials.

activities.differentiation: Use simple, clear language and visual icons for making vs absorbing food.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students can state that mushrooms absorb food while plants make it.
materials: High-quality photos of plants and mushrooms
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes introduction, 20 minutes comparing photos, 15 minutes filling out the chart together.
activities.safety: Use photos only; do not bring wild mushrooms into the classroom to avoid toxic exposure.
activities.task: Compare a mushroom and a plant using photos, focusing on how they get food (making it vs absorbing it).

activities.differentiation: Highlight key words (e.g., sunlight, decomposing) in the case studies for struggling readers.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly identify fungi by noting they absorb food from decomposing matter.
materials: Case study cards with organism descriptions
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes instruction, 30 minutes analyzing cases in groups, 15 minutes sharing justifications.
activities.task: Analyze case studies of different organisms and justify if they are plants or fungi based on their food source.

activities.differentiation: Provide a graphic organizer for students to structure their justification.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student states fungi are not plants and cites their heterotrophic nature and absorptive feeding method.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instructions, 25 minutes writing justification, 10 minutes collection.
activities.task: Decide whether a mushroom is a plant or not, and justify your answer using evidence about how it gets its food.

activities.differentiation: Use large, highly detailed models for better visibility.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students can point to the correct body part on a model when a locomotion type is named.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes introduction, 20 minutes examining models, 10 minutes guided questioning.
activities.safety: Ensure models do not have sharp edges.
activities.task: Introduce locomotion types (swim, fly, walk) and corresponding body parts (fins, wings, legs) using animal models.

context_tasks.protected-areas: Match common local animals from various Salvadoran environments to their primary movement method and identify the body part used.

activities.differentiation: Provide a word bank for body parts and movement types.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly match the local animal to its movement and body part.
materials: Worksheets with images of common local animals
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instruction, 25 minutes matching, 10 minutes review.
activities.task: Match supplied animal pictures to their primary movement method and identify the body part used.

activities.differentiation: Provide mix-and-match templates of animal parts for students to assemble.
activities.mastery_criterion: The drawn animal has clear body parts (e.g., wings) that match the student's stated locomotion method.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instruction, 25 minutes designing, 10 minutes sharing designs.
activities.task: Design an imaginary animal with specific body parts adapted for a chosen method of locomotion.

activities.differentiation: Work in small groups with teacher guidance for students needing support.
activities.mastery_criterion: Cards are sorted correctly and the correct body part is circled on each.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instruction, 20 minutes sorting and circling, 10 minutes checking answers.
activities.task: Sort animal picture cards by locomotion type and circle the body part that allows it using a dry-erase marker.

activities.differentiation: Provide pre-drawn chart structures.
activities.mastery_criterion: Chart accurately categorizes animals and lists fins, wings, and legs respectively.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instruction, 25 minutes creating charts, 10 minutes display.
activities.task: Create a chart categorizing animals into swimmers, flyers, and walkers, listing the key body part for each group.

activities.differentiation: Read instructions aloud and ensure clear, large images.
activities.mastery_criterion: Passes if unfamiliar animals are matched correctly with the corresponding body part identified.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes instructions, 20 minutes completing assessment, 5 minutes collection.
activities.task: Given pictures of unfamiliar animals (e.g., an axolotl, an ostrich), infer their primary movement method and circle the body part.

activities.differentiation: Use color-coded backgrounds for the three diet types to aid memory.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students can define the three diet types based on the pictures shown.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes introduction, 20 minutes matching animals to meals, 10 minutes summarizing.
activities.task: Introduce herbivores, carnivores, and omnivores using pictures of animals and their typical meals.

activities.differentiation: Highlight the food words in the descriptions for easier identification.
activities.mastery_criterion: Animals are correctly placed into herbivore, carnivore, or omnivore categories.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instruction, 25 minutes classifying, 10 minutes review.
activities.task: Classify a list of animals into diet categories based on short written descriptions of what they eat.

activities.differentiation: Provide a list of food items for students to choose from rather than generating their own.
activities.mastery_criterion: Menus accurately reflect plant-based foods for herbivores, meat for carnivores, and both for omnivores.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instruction, 25 minutes creating menus, 10 minutes sharing.
activities.task: Create a restaurant menu for different animal types, ensuring the food items match their specific diet classification.

activities.differentiation: Provide reference cards showing what each animal eats.
activities.mastery_criterion: All cards/cutouts are placed in the correct diet zone based on prior knowledge of their diets.
materials: Printed animal cards or paper for cutouts
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instruction, 25 minutes sorting, 10 minutes group check.
activities.task: Sort printed animal cards or student-drawn cutouts into three distinct habitat zones labeled Herbivore, Carnivore, and Omnivore.

activities.differentiation: Reduce the number of cards for students who need more time.
activities.mastery_criterion: Cards are sorted correctly within the time limit.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes distribution, 10 minutes sorting, 5 minutes checking.
activities.task: Quick sorting of animal diet cards into three piles: herbivore, carnivore, omnivore.

activities.differentiation: Provide a word bank at the top of the worksheet.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly fill in herbivore, carnivore, or omnivore for each item.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes distribution, 10 minutes completing worksheet, 5 minutes review.
activities.task: Fill-in-the-blank worksheet where students write the correct diet classification next to an animal's name and food source.

activities.differentiation: Read the descriptions aloud for the class.
activities.mastery_criterion: Passes if all three animals are correctly classified according to their described diets.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes instructions, 20 minutes completing assessment, 5 minutes collection.
activities.task: Read the descriptions of what a cow, a lion, and a bear eat. Classify each as a herbivore, carnivore, or omnivore.

activities.differentiation: Use clear, contrasting examples (e.g., dog vs. tiger) before introducing nuanced ones.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students can explain that domestic animals rely on humans while wild animals survive in nature.
materials: Pictures of domestic and wild animals
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes introduction, 20 minutes sorting pictures on the board, 15 minutes discussion.
activities.task: Define domestic vs. wild animals, focusing on human care and natural habitats, using picture examples.

activities.differentiation: Provide sentence frames for justifications.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly identify wild animals in the scenarios and justify why they should not be pets.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes instruction, 30 minutes group analysis, 15 minutes presenting justifications.
activities.task: Analyze scenarios of finding different animals and justify whether they can be taken home as pets.

activities.differentiation: Assign specific roles in the discussion group to ensure all students participate.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students articulate that removing animals harms the ecosystem and the animal's well-being.
materials: Discussion prompts related to protected areas
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes setup and context, 30 minutes discussion, 15 minutes summarizing.
activities.task: Group discussion on the impact of taking wild animals from national protected areas to keep as pets.

activities.differentiation: Provide pre-printed images for students to paste into their brochures.
activities.mastery_criterion: Brochure includes at least one valid reason (e.g., need for space, natural diet) why wild animals shouldn't be pets.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instruction, 25 minutes creating brochures, 10 minutes sharing.
activities.task: Create an informational brochure explaining why wild animals are not pets, using evidence about their needs.

activities.differentiation: Use icons next to text for non-readers.
activities.mastery_criterion: Needs are correctly sorted, demonstrating understanding of the difference in survival strategies.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instruction, 25 minutes sorting, 10 minutes review.
activities.task: Sort a list of animal needs into 'Provided by Humans' (domestic) and 'Found in Nature' (wild).

activities.differentiation: Allow students to dictate their justification.
activities.mastery_criterion: Passes if the student decides against keeping the wild animal and provides a justification based on its natural habitat.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instructions, 25 minutes writing, 10 minutes collection.
activities.task: Decide whether a monkey found in the forest should be taken home as a pet. Justify your answer using evidence.

activities.differentiation: Use clear cause-and-effect visual maps on the board.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students can name at least one human threat and one corresponding protective action.
materials: Images of human impacts on nature
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes introduction, 20 minutes discussing images, 15 minutes brainstorming actions.
activities.safety: Ensure images are age-appropriate and not overly distressing.
activities.task: Discuss human threats to wildlife (e.g., littering, feeding) and introduce concrete conservation actions.

activities.differentiation: Provide a list of bad behaviors for students to convert into positive rules.
activities.mastery_criterion: Rules directly address mitigating human threats (e.g., no littering, stay on trails).
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes instruction, 30 minutes drafting rules in groups, 15 minutes presenting.
activities.task: Draft a set of rules for visitors to national protected areas to ensure wild animals are protected.

activities.differentiation: Provide scripts for students who need support with dialogue.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students acting as rangers clearly state a rule that protects wildlife during the role-play.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes assigning roles and prep, 30 minutes role-playing, 15 minutes debrief.
activities.task: Role-play park rangers explaining conservation rules to visitors who are acting carelessly.

activities.differentiation: Provide templates with borders and suggested icons.
activities.mastery_criterion: Sign includes a clear visual and text rule that protects wildlife.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instruction, 25 minutes designing signs, 10 minutes gallery walk.
activities.task: Design a warning sign for a forest to remind people how to protect the animals living there.

activities.differentiation: Work through the first scenario together as a class.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly match the consequence and propose a protective alternative action.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instruction, 25 minutes completing worksheet, 10 minutes review.
activities.task: Match scenarios of human actions in nature to their consequences for wildlife, then propose a better action.

activities.differentiation: Allow students to dictate their response.
activities.mastery_criterion: Passes if the response correctly identifies the harm of feeding wild animals and proposes a safe alternative like observing.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instructions, 25 minutes writing, 10 minutes collection.
activities.task: Read a scenario where a visitor wants to feed a wild animal. Write a response explaining why they shouldn't and what they should do instead.

activities.differentiation: Provide tactile exploration for students with visual impairments.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students can point to and name the roots, stem, and leaves on the live plant.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins intro, 15 mins observation, 10 mins labeling.
activities.safety: Ensure students are not allergic to the plant.
activities.task: Introduce the basic parts of a plant (roots, stem, leaves) using a live potted plant.

activities.differentiation: Provide pre-drawn outlines for students who struggle with fine motor skills.
activities.mastery_criterion: Drawing includes roots, stem, and leaves, all correctly labeled.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instruction, 20 mins drawing, 10 mins sharing.
activities.task: Draw a plant and label its basic parts (roots, stem, leaves).

activities.differentiation: Use clear visual icons for 'helpful' and 'harmful'.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students can name one useful and one harmful aspect of fungi.
materials: Pictures of edible mushrooms, mold on bread, and medicinal fungi
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins intro, 15 mins discussing pictures, 10 mins summary.
activities.safety: Do not bring real mold or toxic fungi into the classroom.
activities.task: Introduce the uses of fungi (e.g., food, medicine) and their potential harms (e.g., diseases, toxicity) using pictures.

activities.differentiation: Read cards aloud for students with reading difficulties.
activities.mastery_criterion: Cards are correctly sorted into helpful and harmful categories.
materials: Scenario cards (e.g., 'eating a mushroom pizza', 'getting a rash from a fungus')
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instruction, 20 mins sorting, 10 mins review.
activities.task: Sort scenario cards into 'Helpful Fungi' and 'Harmful Fungi' categories.

activities.differentiation: Provide pre-marked string for students who struggle with holding the string and marking simultaneously.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students successfully wrap the string, mark it accurately, and read the measurement on the ruler within 1 cm of accuracy.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes for demonstration, 15 minutes for guided student practice, 5 minutes for recording results.
activities.safety: Ensure students do not wrap string around fingers or necks.
activities.task: Demonstrate how to wrap a string around a spherical fruit, mark the meeting point, and measure the string segment with a ruler. Have students replicate the process with an orange.

activities.differentiation: Offer objects of vastly different sizes to challenge advanced students to manage longer string segments.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students record at least 5 accurate measurements, demonstrating proper string alignment and ruler usage.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes setup, 40 minutes of active measuring and recording, 10 minutes sharing results.
activities.safety: Clear floor space to prevent tripping while gathering objects.
activities.task: Students work in pairs to measure the circumference of various classroom objects (globes, balls, thick markers) using string and rulers, recording their data in a table.

activities.differentiation: Provide magnifying glasses for students who need help reading the small millimeter lines on the ruler.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly identify the crop with the largest circumference based on their accurate string measurements.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes introduction and material distribution, 35 minutes measuring, 10 minutes conclusion.
activities.safety: Ensure crops are clean and free of sharp edges or pests.
activities.task: Students measure the circumference of different local crops (like small pumpkins or large maize cobs) using string and rulers to determine which crop has the largest girth.

activities.differentiation: Allow verbal reporting of the measurement for students with writing difficulties.
activities.mastery_criterion: The recorded measurement is within 1 cm of the actual circumference and the string method is used correctly.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes instructions, 20 minutes individual assessment, 5 minutes collection.
activities.safety: Standard classroom safety; no eating the fruits.
activities.task: Provide students with a spherical fruit, a piece of string, and a ruler. Ask them to determine the distance around the thickest part of the fruit and record the measurement in centimeters.

activities.differentiation: Pre-punch holes in the paper cups for students with fine motor challenges.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students successfully assemble a hanger balance that hangs level when empty.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes demonstration, 20 minutes guided construction, 10 minutes testing equilibrium.
activities.safety: Ensure string is cut with safety scissors; monitor to prevent swallowing marbles.
activities.task: Guide students step-by-step to build a balance using a clothes hanger, string, and two cups. Demonstrate how to find equilibrium using identical marbles.

activities.differentiation: Provide heavier objects for advanced students to require counting larger quantities of marbles.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students accurately record the number of marbles required to balance at least 4 different objects.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes setup, 40 minutes weighing and recording, 10 minutes cleanup.
activities.safety: Keep marbles in containers when not in use to prevent slipping hazards.
activities.task: Students use their constructed balances to compare the mass of various classroom items (erasers, pencils, glue sticks) against a standard non-standard unit (marbles), recording the equivalents.

context_tasks.dollar-budget: Students use their balances to determine the mass of hypothetical household items purchased with a hypothetical dollar budget, using coins as the non-standard mass unit.

activities.differentiation: Pair students so one can stabilize the hanger while the other adds coins.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students successfully balance the items with coins and record the mass in 'coin units'.
materials: Small household items (e.g., small soap, sponge)
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes context introduction, 35 minutes balancing activity, 10 minutes discussion.
activities.safety: Ensure plastic coins are large enough to not be choking hazards.
activities.task: Use a balance to compare the masses of two supplied objects using identical counters as a non-standard unit. Record the counter counts; do not infer mass from monetary value.

activities.differentiation: Provide visual step-by-step cards for the construction phase.
activities.mastery_criterion: The balance is constructed symmetrically and the student correctly identifies the equilibrium point with the correct number of marbles.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 25 minutes construction, 15 minutes measurement, 5 minutes recording.
activities.safety: Monitor use of scissors and small objects.
activities.task: Ask students to build a balance using a clothes hanger, string, and two cups, and then determine how many marbles equal the mass of a small eraser.

activities.differentiation: Allow peer assistance for tying knots.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students assemble the balance correctly and achieve equilibrium within the time limit.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes instructions, 20 minutes assembly and testing, 5 minutes review.
activities.task: Students quickly reassemble a balance from disassembled parts and verify its equilibrium using identical wooden blocks.

activities.differentiation: Use larger beads for students with fine motor difficulties.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly add beads one by one until the hanger is level.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes setup, 20 minutes measuring, 5 minutes cleanup.
activities.safety: Ensure rocks are clean and beads are not swallowed.
activities.task: Students use a pre-made balance to find the mass of a small rock in terms of plastic beads, recalling the procedure for achieving equilibrium.

activities.differentiation: Provide pre-folded paper for students to observe if they cannot fold it themselves.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students can articulate that the folded bridge holds more weight and identify the folds as the reason for increased strength.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes demonstration, 15 minutes guided student replication, 10 minutes discussion of reasoning.
activities.safety: Ensure falling coins do not pinch fingers.
activities.task: Demonstrate how to build a flat paper bridge and a fan-folded paper bridge between two books. Show how to add coins to the center until collapse.

activities.differentiation: Provide a template with folding lines for students who need structural guidance.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students record data accurately and reason that more folds generally increase structural resistance up to a point.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes setup, 40 minutes experimentation and data collection, 10 minutes reasoning writing.
activities.safety: Keep workspace clear of clutter to manage falling coins.
activities.task: Students experiment with different numbers of folds in their paper bridges (e.g., 2 folds vs. 6 folds) and record how many coins each can hold, justifying which design is best.

activities.differentiation: Allow verbal justification for students who struggle with writing.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students justify the folded design's strength using evidence from their block count data.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes context and setup, 35 minutes testing, 10 minutes writing justification.
activities.safety: Ensure blocks are lightweight to prevent injury upon bridge collapse.
activities.task: Students test flat vs. folded bridges using small blocks instead of coins, simulating a road over a water sanitation channel, and write a justification for the strongest design.

activities.differentiation: Provide a sentence starter for the justification portion.
activities.mastery_criterion: The student records that the folded bridge holds significantly more coins and justifies that the folds make the paper stiffer.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes instructions, 25 minutes testing, 10 minutes writing conclusion.
activities.task: Have students place coins one by one on the center of a flat paper bridge until it collapses, then repeat with a fan-folded bridge, and state which design is stronger and why based on data.

activities.differentiation: Use a visual diagram showing electricity turning into heat for visual learners.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students explicitly link the visual observation of the melting wax to the generation of heat, stating that electrical energy from the battery transforms into thermal energy.
materials: Small piece of wax or butter
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes safety briefing and setup, 10 minutes demonstration, 10 minutes discussion and identification.
activities.safety: Teacher-only handling of the circuit. Students must not touch the hot graphite and should only observe from a safe distance. Ensure no flammable materials are nearby.
activities.task: Perform a teacher-led demonstration connecting a battery to a pencil lead with a small piece of wax on it. Have students observe the wax melting as a visual indicator of heat and identify the energy change.

activities.differentiation: Provide a word bank (electrical, thermal, mechanical, light) for the worksheet.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly identify electrical to thermal energy for the graphite, and electrical to mechanical/light for the others.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes per demonstration (45 mins total), 15 minutes worksheet completion.
activities.safety: Teacher controls all circuits. Students observe from a safe distance.
activities.task: Students observe a series of safe, teacher-led demonstrations (e.g., a small battery-operated fan, a flashlight, and the graphite circuit) and identify the energy transformations in each.

activities.differentiation: Include appliances with obvious heat outputs (like a toaster glowing red) for easier identification.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly label the input (electrical) and output (thermal) energy for at least 3 appliances.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes review of the concept, 35 minutes diagram labeling, 10 minutes peer review.
activities.safety: No physical appliances used, only paper diagrams.
activities.task: Students review diagrams of household appliances (toaster, iron, heater) and identify that they all transform electrical energy into thermal energy, similar to the graphite experiment.

activities.differentiation: Allow students to draw the transformation if they cannot write the words.
activities.mastery_criterion: The student states that electrical energy from the battery is changing into thermal energy (heat) in the pencil lead, using the melting wax as evidence.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes demonstration, 20 minutes individual recording of the answer.
activities.safety: Strict adult supervision; students do not touch the circuit and observe from a safe distance.
activities.task: Show students a safe, teacher-led demonstration of a battery connected to a pencil lead with a small piece of wax on it. Ask them to observe the wax melting and name the type of energy transformation occurring.

activities.differentiation: Provide pre-assembled central rubber band mechanisms for students with fine motor delays.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students successfully assemble the device and demonstrate that twisting the rubber band causes it to roll.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 20 minutes guided assembly, 15 minutes testing, 10 minutes explanation of elastic energy.
activities.safety: Ensure rubber bands are in good condition to prevent snapping.
activities.task: Guide students to build a rolling device using CDs, a cardboard tube, and rubber bands. Demonstrate how twisting the rubber band stores energy for motion.

activities.differentiation: Pair students so one counts twists while the other measures distance.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students successfully operate the device and record that more twists result in a longer rolling distance.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes setup, 40 minutes testing and measuring, 10 minutes sharing results.
activities.safety: Ensure a clear path for rolling devices to prevent tripping.
activities.task: Students experiment with their elastic devices by twisting the rubber band a specific number of times (e.g., 5, 10, 15) and measuring how far the device rolls.

activities.differentiation: Provide pre-weighed packets to tape on for consistency.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students successfully modify the device, operate it, and observe changes in motion.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes modification, 35 minutes testing, 10 minutes cleanup.
activities.safety: Ensure weights are securely taped so they do not fly off during motion.
activities.task: Students modify their elastic devices by adding weight (e.g., taping coins to the tube) to see how mass affects the motion generated by the twisted rubber band.

activities.differentiation: Provide visual step-by-step instructions during the assessment.
activities.mastery_criterion: The device is assembled correctly and demonstrates motion upon release.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 30 minutes assembly, 15 minutes individual demonstration to the teacher.
activities.task: Instruct students to build a rolling device using CDs, a cardboard tube, and rubber bands, twist the rubber band mechanism, and release it on the floor to demonstrate motion.

activities.differentiation: Use highly familiar local animals for examples.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students can verbally state the difference between domestic and wild animals based on human reliance.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes explanation, 10 minutes guided group sorting.
activities.task: Present images of common animals. Explain the difference between domestic (rely on humans) and wild (survive independently). Sort a few examples together on the board.

activities.differentiation: Provide cards with both pictures and words for early readers.
activities.mastery_criterion: Groups correctly sort at least 18 out of 20 cards based on human reliance.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes instructions, 30 minutes group sorting, 10 minutes class review.
activities.task: Students work in small groups to sort a deck of 20 animal cards into 'domestic' and 'wild' piles, discussing their reasoning for each.

context_tasks.protected-areas: Students draw one domestic animal and one wild animal found in El Salvador (e.g., iguanas, tacuacines, or various birds), writing one sentence for each explaining how it gets its food.

activities.differentiation: Provide sentence starters: 'The [animal] gets food from...'
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly identify the food source (human provided vs. independently found).
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes context discussion, 25 minutes drawing and writing, 10 minutes sharing.
activities.task: Compare supplied pictures and habitat records for one domestic and one wild animal. Draw each and describe how it obtains food using the supplied evidence.

activities.differentiation: Read the list of animals aloud for students who need reading support.
activities.mastery_criterion: All animals are correctly categorized and the reasoning references human dependence vs. independent survival.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes instructions, 15 minutes independent work.
activities.task: Provide a list of animals (e.g., dog, chicken, iguana, bee). Ask the student to sort them into 'domestic' and 'wild' categories and provide one reason for their sorting.

activities.differentiation: Allow students with mobility issues to point left or right instead of walking.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students consistently move to the correct side of the room based on the animal's classification.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes rules explanation, 15 minutes active gameplay.
activities.safety: Ensure clear pathways to prevent tripping while moving.
activities.task: Play a quick game where the teacher calls out an animal name and students move to the left side of the room for 'domestic' and the right side for 'wild'.

activities.differentiation: Use high-contrast images for visually impaired students.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly draw lines matching the animals to their appropriate habitat icons.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes distribution, 10 minutes completion, 5 minutes self-correction.
activities.task: Students complete a quick matching worksheet connecting pictures of animals to either a 'house/farm' icon (domestic) or a 'forest/jungle' icon (wild).

activities.differentiation: Provide pre-cut straws for students with severe fine motor limitations.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students successfully cut straws to the correct length and pack them so they do not fall out when the can is inverted.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes demonstration, 25 minutes guided construction, 5 minutes inversion test.
activities.safety: Ensure cans have no sharp edges. Monitor scissor use.
activities.task: Demonstrate how to measure and cut paper straws to the length of a recycled can, and pack them tightly inside to create hollow spaces for insects.

activities.differentiation: Allow students to work in pairs to hold the carton while packing.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students adapt their packing technique to the new shape, ensuring materials are secure and provide hollow spaces.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes material selection, 35 minutes construction, 10 minutes cleanup.
activities.safety: Teacher handles pruning shears if twigs are thick. Ensure cartons are washed.
activities.task: Students build a second insect hotel using a different container shape (e.g., a square milk carton) and natural materials like hollow twigs, ensuring tight packing.

activities.differentiation: Provide double-sided tape as an alternative to liquid glue for less mess.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students successfully attach natural camouflage to the exterior without blocking the hollow tube entrances.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instruction, 40 minutes decorating, 10 minutes drying and cleanup.
activities.safety: Ensure glue is non-toxic and students wash hands after handling natural materials.
activities.task: Students decorate the outside of their insect hotels using natural materials (leaves, bark) glued to the exterior to help it blend into a natural environment.

activities.differentiation: Mark a line on the straws for students who struggle with measuring the length.
activities.mastery_criterion: The tubes are cut to size and packed tightly enough to stay in place when the can is tilted.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes instructions, 30 minutes independent construction, 5 minutes teacher checking.
activities.safety: Check cans for sharp edges before assessment.
activities.task: Ask students to create an insect shelter by cutting paper straws to the length of a recycled can and packing them tightly inside.

activities.differentiation: Use clear, contrasting images to make the difference in traffic obvious.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students verbally identify the quiet garden and reason that insects avoid human disturbance.
materials: Pictures of high-traffic and low-traffic areas
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes discussion of insect needs, 10 minutes scenario analysis.
activities.task: Discuss why insects need quiet places. Show pictures of a busy playground and a quiet garden corner, asking students to infer which is better for an insect hotel and why.

activities.differentiation: Pair students to collaborate on one map if drawing is challenging.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students select a viable low-traffic spot and note its quiet nature on their map.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 25 minutes schoolyard walk and selection, 15 minutes mapping, 5 minutes return.
activities.safety: Keep students within designated safe boundaries of the schoolyard.
activities.task: Take students on a walk around the schoolyard. Have them select a specific spot for their insect hotel and draw a map marking the location, noting why it is low-traffic.

activities.differentiation: Highlight the human paths in a bright color to help visual processing.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students place the 'X' away from paths and playgrounds, justifying it with the need to avoid disturbance.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes map reading instruction, 25 minutes independent work, 10 minutes sharing.
activities.task: Students review a map of a hypothetical park and mark an 'X' where they would place an insect hotel, writing a justification based on avoiding human paths.

activities.differentiation: Allow verbal justification for students who cannot write a full sentence.
activities.mastery_criterion: The chosen location is low-traffic and the justification explicitly mentions avoiding disturbance to the insects.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes instructions, 15 minutes writing.
activities.task: Ask students to choose a location in the schoolyard or at home to place their insect hotel and write one sentence explaining why that location is best for the insects.

activities.differentiation: Provide pre-measured cups of rocks and soil to simplify the layering process.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students successfully replicate the layers (rocks, then soil) and plant their specimen securely.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes demonstration, 25 minutes guided construction, 5 minutes cleanup.
activities.safety: Ensure students wash hands thoroughly after handling soil. Do not use soil with chemical fertilizers.
activities.task: Demonstrate how to layer small rocks for drainage, add soil, and carefully plant a small specimen in a clear plastic container to create a terrarium.

activities.differentiation: Use spray bottles instead of watering cans to prevent accidental overwatering by students with poor motor control.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students successfully water the plant without flooding it, observing the drainage layer's function.
materials: Small watering cans or spray bottles
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes decoration, 20 minutes watering and observation, 25 minutes drawing their terrarium.
activities.safety: Wipe up any spilled water immediately to prevent slipping.
activities.task: Students add decorative elements (small plastic animals, colored stones) to their terrariums and lightly water the soil, observing how the water drains into the rock layer.

activities.differentiation: Mark a line on the cup to show how much soil is needed.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly layer rocks and soil, and plant the seed at the correct depth.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instruction, 40 minutes construction and planting, 10 minutes cleanup.
activities.safety: Ensure seeds are not treated with toxic fungicides (use food-grade or untreated seeds). Wash hands after.
activities.task: Students build a second, smaller terrarium using a plastic cup, focusing on planting a seed (like maize) instead of a live plant, ensuring the soil depth is appropriate.

activities.differentiation: Provide verbal prompts for the order of layers if a student freezes.
activities.mastery_criterion: The terrarium has distinct layers (rocks then soil) and the plant is securely placed in the soil with roots covered.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes instructions, 30 minutes independent construction, 10 minutes cleanup and teacher evaluation.
activities.task: Provide students with a clear plastic container, small rocks, soil, and a small plant. Ask them to assemble a terrarium that supports the plant's growth.

activities.differentiation: Provide a smaller, high-contrast version of the poster for students with visual impairments.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student points to and names at least three objects that pose a risk in the poster.
materials: Large poster of a messy classroom
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes for introduction, 20 minutes for guided identification and discussion, 10 minutes for summarizing.
activities.safety: Ensure the actual classroom floor is clear of tripping hazards during the activity.
activities.task: Display a large poster of a messy classroom. Guide students to point out objects that could cause someone to trip, fall, or get hurt. Discuss why each identified object is a risk.

activities.differentiation: Pair students to discuss the cards before sorting.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly sorts all unsafe situation cards into the risk pile.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes explaining the sorting rules, 20 minutes of sorting, 10 minutes reviewing answers as a class.
activities.safety: Use laminated cards with rounded corners to prevent paper cuts.
activities.task: Students sort illustrated cards into two piles: safe situations and unsafe situations (risks).

activities.differentiation: Provide photographs with fewer objects for students who get easily overwhelmed by visual clutter.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student circles at least three distinct risks across the provided photographs.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes distributing materials and explaining, 20 minutes of independent work, 10 minutes of peer review.
activities.safety: Ensure dry-erase markers are non-toxic and used in a ventilated area.
activities.task: Students view photographs of different rooms in a house and circle the accident risks using a dry-erase marker.

activities.differentiation: Allow students to verbally describe the risks they want to draw if fine motor skills are developing.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student successfully draws three recognizable risks and identifies the risks in their partner's drawing.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 20 minutes for drawing, 10 minutes for trading and finding, 10 minutes for class sharing.
activities.safety: Standard classroom safety with drawing materials.
activities.task: Students draw a picture of a playground and intentionally include three accident risks, then trade with a partner to find them.

activities.differentiation: Read instructions aloud and allow pointing instead of circling for students needing motor support.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student circles a spilled liquid, an open cabinet door, and a tripping hazard.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes setup, 20 minutes for independent completion, 5 minutes collection.
activities.task: Provide a worksheet with an image of a messy kitchen. Students must independently circle three things that could cause an accident.

context_tasks.seismic-risk: Bridge the concept of physical risks (like tripping, learned previously) to natural events. Use wooden blocks to build a tall, unstable tower representing a local hazard (like the San Salvador volcano or a local fault line). Place a toy figure far away, then close to it. Explain that the hazard is the event itself, but the risk (probability of harm) changes based on where the figure stands.

activities.differentiation: Use larger, brightly colored blocks for better visibility.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student can verbally state that the tower is the hazard and standing close is the risk.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes demonstration, 15 minutes guided discussion, 10 minutes checking for understanding.
activities.safety: Ensure the block tower is small enough not to cause injury when it falls.
activities.task: Use a teacher-prepared diagram of a tall unstable block tower and objects placed near or far from it. Distinguish the possible falling event from the exposure of an object to that event. Do not shake or climb a real structure.

activities.differentiation: Provide fewer pairs to match for students who need a modified workload.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly pairs the hazard cards with their corresponding risk definition cards.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instruction, 20 minutes matching activity, 10 minutes review.
activities.task: Students match cards showing a natural event (hazard) with cards showing the probability of harm (risk) based on human location.

context_tasks.seismic-risk: Read scenarios about local Salvadoran hazards (e.g., earthquakes on the San Salvador fault, heavy rains in vulnerable areas). Students hold up a red card if the scenario describes a hazard, and a yellow card if it describes a risk.

activities.differentiation: Provide visual cues on the cards (e.g., a warning sign on red, a person on yellow).
activities.mastery_criterion: Student holds up the correct card for at least 4 out of 5 scenarios.
materials: Red and yellow construction paper cards
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes explaining the rules, 20 minutes reading scenarios and voting, 10 minutes discussing the answers.
activities.safety: Ensure students remain seated while holding up cards to avoid collisions.
activities.task: Read fictional cards describing a hazardous event and cards describing exposure to that event. Sort event and exposure cards, then justify one pairing.

activities.differentiation: Read the options aloud for students with reading difficulties.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student selects the option defining risk as the probability of suffering harmful consequences.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes setup and reading instructions, 15 minutes independent work, 5 minutes collection.
activities.task: Students complete a multiple-choice question selecting the correct definition of 'risk' from three options.

activities.differentiation: Allow students to use hand signals instead of standing/sitting if mobility is an issue.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly identifies the difference through physical movement.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes explaining rules, 15 minutes playing the game.
activities.safety: Ensure chairs are pushed in to prevent tripping when standing and sitting.
activities.task: Quick recall game: The teacher says a word (either a hazard like 'rain' or a risk like 'flooded house'). Students stand up for hazard, sit down for risk.

activities.differentiation: Allow verbal dictation to the teacher for students who struggle with writing.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student's sentence includes the concept of probability of harm or getting hurt.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes distributing paper, 10 minutes writing, 5 minutes collecting at the door.
activities.task: Exit ticket: Students write or dictate one sentence explaining what a risk is before leaving for recess.

activities.differentiation: Provide alternative protective postures for students using wheelchairs.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student successfully demonstrates dropping, covering their head/neck, and holding onto a sturdy object.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes explanation and demonstration, 20 minutes guided practice, 10 minutes debrief.
activities.safety: Ensure desks are stable and floors are clear of sharp objects before students drop.
activities.task: Demonstrate the 'Drop, Cover, and Hold on' technique for earthquakes. Explain each step clearly. Have students practice the motion step-by-step under their desks.

activities.differentiation: Give a visual warning (like flashing lights) slightly before the verbal cue for students with auditory processing delays.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student reacts promptly and correctly assumes the safe position without prompting.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes setting expectations, 30 minutes of embedded practice during another light activity, 5 minutes review.
activities.safety: Remind students not to run or push others when moving to take cover.
activities.task: Role-play activity: The teacher calls out 'Earthquake!' at random times during a 30-minute period. Students must immediately execute the safe action.

activities.differentiation: Provide pre-drawn characters that students can cut and paste into the panels.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student's comic accurately depicts a recognized safety measure in the middle panel.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instruction, 25 minutes drawing, 10 minutes sharing comics.
activities.task: Students create a simple three-panel comic strip showing a character feeling an earthquake, taking cover, and waiting safely.

activities.differentiation: Number the backs of the cards so students can self-check their sequence.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student places the evacuation steps in a logical, safe order for the given hazard.
materials: Sets of sequence cards covering multiple hazards
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes explanation, 20 minutes sequencing, 15 minutes discussing why the order matters.
activities.task: Students sequence a set of mixed-up picture cards showing the steps of an emergency evacuation plan for various hazards, including earthquakes, floods, and landslides.

activities.differentiation: Allow verbal responses for students who cannot draw or write clearly.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student draws or writes about a recognized safety measure for floods, such as moving to higher ground.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes instructions, 20 minutes independent work, 5 minutes collection.
activities.task: Present a novel scenario: a heavy rainstorm causes a flood warning near their home. Students draw or write one safe action they should take in this specific context.

context_tasks.water-sanitation: Relate the activity to local issues like landslides in Nejapa or sedimentation of the Lempa River. Set up three plastic bottle halves: one with bare soil, one with dead leaves, one with live plants. Pour equal amounts of water through each. Ask students to observe the runoff water color and infer why the plant bottle has clear water, protecting the 'hillside'.

activities.differentiation: Provide magnifying glasses for students to closely examine the roots holding the soil.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student states that the roots hold the soil, preventing it from washing away.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes setup and hypothesis, 20 minutes conducting the pour, 25 minutes discussion and reasoning.
activities.safety: Ensure any cut plastic edges are taped to prevent scratches. Clean up water spills immediately to prevent slipping.
activities.task: Relate the activity to local issues like landslides in Nejapa or sedimentation of the the supplied location River. Set up three plastic bottle halves: one with bare soil, one with dead leaves, one with live plants. Pour equal amounts of water through each. Ask students to observe the runoff water color and infer why the plant bottle has clear water, protecting the 'hillside'.

activities.differentiation: Assign specific roles (pourer, observer, recorder) to ensure all students participate according to their strengths.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student infers that a steeper angle causes more soil to wash away, but plants still offer the best protection.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes setup, 25 minutes experimenting, 20 minutes comparing results with the flat model.
activities.safety: Wipe up any spilled water immediately.
activities.task: Students repeat the erosion model experiment, but this time they tilt the bottles at a steeper angle to simulate a steep hill. They observe and discuss how the angle affects the amount of soil washed away.

activities.differentiation: Provide pre-drawn observation charts for students to color in the darkness of the water.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student reasons that faster water flow carries more soil away.
materials: Watering can with a sprinkle spout
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instruction, 30 minutes conducting the two pours, 20 minutes reasoning discussion.
activities.safety: Conduct the activity outdoors or over a large plastic tarp to manage mud.
activities.task: Students test the erosion model by pouring water very slowly (light rain) versus very quickly (heavy storm) into the bare soil bottle, comparing the runoff.

activities.differentiation: Use highly contrasting soil colors (e.g., dark potting soil vs light sand) for clear visual results.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student observes and states which soil type resulted in dirtier runoff water.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes preparing the new soils, 25 minutes testing, 20 minutes discussing findings.
activities.safety: Ensure students wash hands thoroughly after handling soil.
activities.task: Students compare the erosion of regular garden soil versus sandy soil in the bare-soil model, observing which washes away faster.

activities.differentiation: Allow students to use gestures (like interlacing fingers) to explain how roots hold soil if they lack the vocabulary.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student selects the bare dirt hill and provides a logical justification involving the lack of roots to hold the soil.
materials: Pictures of a bare hill and a forested hill
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes setup, 25 minutes conducting individual verbal assessments, 5 minutes wrap-up.
activities.task: Show the student a picture of a steep, bare dirt hill and a picture of a hill covered in grass and trees. Ask them to predict which hill will lose more soil during a heavy rainstorm and explain why using their knowledge of roots.

activities.differentiation: Use bins with distinct colors (e.g., green for biodegradable, black for non-biodegradable) and picture labels.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student can correctly identify the bin for an apple core and a plastic bottle during the demonstration.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes explanation, 15 minutes guided sorting, 10 minutes review.
activities.safety: Ensure all physical waste items are clean, sanitized, and free of sharp edges.
activities.task: Introduce the concepts of biodegradable (nature breaks it down) and non-biodegradable (nature cannot easily break it down). Show clean examples of each and sort them into two labeled bins as a class.

activities.differentiation: Allow students to walk instead of run, or have the hoops brought to their desks.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student places their assigned cards in the correct hoops.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes explaining rules, 20 minutes playing the relay, 10 minutes checking the hoops together.
activities.safety: Ensure the running path is clear of obstacles to prevent tripping.
activities.task: Relay race: Students pick a picture card of a waste item from a pile and run to drop it in the correct biodegradable or non-biodegradable hoop.

activities.differentiation: Provide pre-cut images for students who struggle with scissor skills.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly categorizes at least 5 items on their T-chart.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes distributing materials, 25 minutes cutting and pasting, 10 minutes sharing.
activities.task: Students cut out pictures of various items from old magazines and paste them onto a T-chart labeled Biodegradable and Non-Biodegradable.

activities.differentiation: Provide templates of biodegradable items to color and attach.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student includes only biodegradable items (like fruit peels, leaves, paper) on their mobile.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instruction, 25 minutes crafting, 5 minutes cleanup.
activities.safety: Teacher should handle the hole punch if it is stiff or pinches.
activities.task: Students create a hanging mobile using only drawings of biodegradable items, reinforcing what belongs in that specific category.

activities.differentiation: Read the bin labels aloud.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly connects the apple core and banana peel to biodegradable, and the plastic bottle and glass jar to non-biodegradable.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes instructions, 20 minutes independent work, 5 minutes collection.
activities.task: Provide a worksheet with images of an apple core, plastic bottle, glass jar, and banana peel. Students draw a line connecting each item to the correct bin (Biodegradable or Non-biodegradable).

activities.differentiation: Use a storyboard with pictures to accompany the verbal story.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student identifies that not washing hands after the bathroom was the poor hygiene practice.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes reading the story, 15 minutes guided discussion, 10 minutes summarizing.
activities.task: Read a short story about a character who forgets to wash their hands after using the bathroom and gets a stomach ache. Discuss the specific action that caused the illness.

activities.differentiation: Provide fewer pictures per page to reduce visual clutter.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly circles the poor hygiene practices (e.g., sneezing into hands, not washing hands).
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instruction, 20 minutes independent work, 10 minutes reviewing as a class.
activities.task: Show a series of pictures depicting daily routines. Students must spot and circle the 'mistake' (the poor hygiene practice) in each picture.

activities.differentiation: Allow students to work in pairs to act out the prompts.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly identifies the acted-out habit as poor hygiene when applicable.
materials: Action prompt cards for the teacher
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes explaining rules, 25 minutes playing charades, 5 minutes wrap-up.
activities.safety: Ensure students have enough space to act out safely without hitting desks.
activities.task: Play a game of charades where students act out either a good hygiene habit or a poor hygiene habit. The class guesses the action and states if it is good or poor.

activities.differentiation: Use cards with clear, simple illustrations and minimal text.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student places cards like 'not washing hands' into the 'Can make us sick' pile.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instruction, 20 minutes sorting, 10 minutes checking answers.
activities.task: Students sort a deck of cards showing various actions into a 'Keeps us healthy' pile and a 'Can make us sick' pile.

activities.differentiation: Provide visual icons next to the numbers to help students keep track of which item is being read.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student marks a sad face for 'Not washing hands after going to the bathroom'.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes setup, 15 minutes reading and marking, 5 minutes collection.
activities.task: Read a list of actions aloud. Students mark a sad face on their paper next to the number if the action represents poor hygiene.

activities.differentiation: Use physical props (like a toy shield) to make the metaphor more concrete.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student can state that vaccines help make defenses to fight sickness.
materials: Drawing of a castle and guards
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes explanation with metaphor, 10 minutes guided Q&A, 5 minutes summary.
activities.task: Explain vaccines using a metaphor: the body is a castle, and vaccines are training for the guards (defenses) so they know how to fight off invaders (sickness).

activities.differentiation: Provide a body outline template for students to draw inside.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student's drawing reflects the concept of protection or defense inside the body.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes instruction, 20 minutes drawing, 5 minutes sharing.
activities.task: Students draw a picture of their body's 'defenses' (like tiny shields or guards) stopping sickness, based on the vaccine metaphor.

activities.differentiation: Number the backs of the cards for self-checking.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student places the pictures in the correct chronological order.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instruction, 15 minutes sequencing, 5 minutes review.
activities.task: Students sequence three pictures: 1) Getting a vaccine, 2) Body making defenses, 3) Staying healthy when sickness is around.

activities.differentiation: Allow verbal responses for students who cannot write a full sentence.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student writes that a vaccine helps the body make defenses or fight off sickness.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes instruction, 20 minutes writing, 5 minutes collection.
activities.task: Ask the student to write one sentence explaining what a vaccine does inside the body.

activities.differentiation: Allow students to pass the ball without speaking if they are non-verbal, pointing to a picture board instead.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student recalls a relevant word associated with vaccine function.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes explaining rules, 15 minutes playing the game.
activities.safety: Ensure the ball is soft and students roll or gently toss it to avoid injury.
activities.task: Pass a soft ball around a circle. When the music stops, the student holding the ball must say one word related to what vaccines do (e.g., 'defenses', 'protect', 'fight').

activities.differentiation: Provide a word bank for students who need spelling support.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student fills in the blank with 'defenses' or a similar accurate term.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes distribution, 10 minutes completion, 5 minutes collection.
activities.task: Provide a quick fill-in-the-blank slip: 'A vaccine helps the body make ________ to fight sickness.'

activities.differentiation: Use highly realistic photos rather than abstract drawings for clarity.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student can point to the foods that require cooking when asked.
materials: Pictures of raw chicken, raw beans, and an apple
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes explanation, 10 minutes guided questioning, 5 minutes summary.
activities.safety: Use pictures only; do not bring raw meat into the classroom.
activities.task: Show pictures of raw chicken, raw beans, and an apple. Explain that while the apple can be washed and eaten raw, the chicken and beans must be cooked to be safe to eat.

activities.differentiation: Limit the number of items to sort for students who need a focused task.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly places items like play-chicken in the 'Must be cooked' basket.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instruction, 15 minutes sorting, 5 minutes review.
activities.safety: Ensure play-food is clean and large enough not to be a choking hazard.
activities.task: Students sort plastic play-food into two baskets: 'Safe to eat raw (after washing)' and 'Must be cooked'.

activities.differentiation: Provide pre-drawn food items for students to color and paste onto their menu.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student draws and correctly identifies which of their drawn items needs cooking.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes instruction, 20 minutes drawing, 5 minutes sharing.
activities.task: Students draw a 'safe menu' consisting of one item that can be eaten raw and one item that must be cooked, labeling them appropriately.

activities.differentiation: Use color-coded borders to help guide the matching process.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly matches the raw ingredients to their cooked counterparts.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instruction, 15 minutes matching, 5 minutes review.
activities.task: Matching game: Students match a picture of a raw ingredient (like raw meat or raw dough) to its safe, cooked final dish.

activities.differentiation: Read the names of the foods aloud as students look at the pictures.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student circles the raw chicken and raw beans.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes instruction, 20 minutes independent work, 5 minutes collection.
activities.task: Provide a worksheet with images of raw chicken, an apple, and raw beans. Students circle the ones that must be cooked before eating.

activities.differentiation: Use a blacklight and fluorescent lotion if available, otherwise the oil and cinnamon provide a high-contrast visual for all students.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student reasons that hands must be washed with soap to remove invisible organisms that spread.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes introduction, 15 minutes demonstration, 15 minutes reasoning discussion.
activities.safety: Ensure no students have allergies to the food items used. Avoid touching faces during the activity.
activities.task: Rub a drop of cooking oil and a pinch of ground cinnamon on a student's hand to represent invisible organisms. Have them try to wash it off with just water, then with soap and water. Discuss why soap is needed to break down the oils that trap dirt and germs, justifying the need for proper handwashing.

activities.differentiation: Provide step-by-step visual instructions at the sink.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student infers that soap is needed to properly remove the 'invisible organisms' represented by the cinnamon.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes setup, 20 minutes experimenting in groups, 10 minutes comparing and discussing.
activities.safety: Ensure water temperature is safe and clean up any spills near the sink to prevent slipping.
activities.task: Students work in pairs. One applies the oil and cinnamon 'germs'. They test washing with cold water only, warm water only, and finally soap and water, observing which method removes the 'germs' best and inferring why soap is essential.

activities.differentiation: Provide a pre-traced hand for students with fine motor difficulties.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student's sentence justifies handwashing by mentioning the removal of organisms or germs.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instruction, 20 minutes drawing and writing, 10 minutes sharing.
activities.task: Students trace their hand on paper and draw tiny 'invisible organisms' all over it, then write one sentence at the bottom explaining why they need to wash them off.

activities.differentiation: Allow students to use a fill-in-the-blank letter template.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student's letter includes the reasoning that invisible things can make us sick.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instruction, 20 minutes writing, 10 minutes reading letters aloud.
activities.task: Students dictate or write a short letter to a friend explaining why they should use soap when washing hands, even if their hands don't look dirty.

activities.differentiation: Conduct the assessment verbally for students who struggle with writing.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student identifies the dish with growth and explains that invisible organisms from unwashed hands were transferred to it.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes instruction, 20 minutes independent work or verbal interviews, 5 minutes wrap-up.
activities.task: Show the student pictures of two petri dishes from a handwashing experiment (one with spots of bacterial growth, one clean). Ask them to infer which dish was touched by unwashed hands and justify their answer based on the presence of invisible organisms.

activities.differentiation: Provide clear, simple verbal instructions and allow students to participate in pairs.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student can explain their role as a defense created by the vaccine.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes explaining the roles, 15 minutes role-playing, 5 minutes debriefing.
activities.safety: Ensure students move safely without running during the role-play.
activities.task: Students role-play as 'body guards' (defenses) learning to recognize a 'villain' (sickness) after being trained by a 'teacher' (vaccine).

activities.differentiation: Provide pre-cut images for students who struggle with scissor skills.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly categorizes at least four food items.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes instruction, 20 minutes cutting and pasting, 5 minutes sharing.
activities.task: Students create a 'safe kitchen' poster by cutting out pictures of food and gluing them under 'Wash and Eat' or 'Cook First' headings.

activities.differentiation: Provide physical labels with unit symbols for students to hold and place next to objects, supporting visual and tactile learners without changing the cognitive task.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly states the unit used for mass, volume, and length when prompted.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins introduction, 20 mins direct instruction with examples, 15 mins guided group identification.
activities.safety: Ensure all containers are empty and clean to prevent spills or allergic reactions.
activities.task: Introduce standard units (g, L, cm) by displaying common household items and explicitly teaching which unit corresponds to mass, volume, and length.

activities.differentiation: Include items with highly distinct properties (e.g., very long string vs. heavy bag of sand) for students needing clearer physical cues.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly sorts at least 8 out of 10 items into the correct measurement station.
materials: Various clean household items (bottles, boxes, string, bags of beans or rice)
Sorting bins labeled g, libras, L, cm
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins setup and instructions, 25 mins active sorting, 10 mins class review and correction.
activities.safety: Use plastic containers instead of glass to prevent breakage.
activities.task: Students sort a variety of everyday items into stations based on whether they are measured in grams, pounds (libras), liters, or centimeters, discussing local market contexts.

activities.differentiation: Read the names of the items aloud for students with reading difficulties, maintaining the requirement to match the unit independently.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly matches at least 4 out of 5 items to their appropriate measurement unit.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instruction, 25 mins independent work, 10 mins collection and transition.
activities.safety: Standard classroom safety; ensure adequate lighting and seating.
activities.task: Students complete a matching task where they draw lines connecting 5 drawn items (milk, cereal, pencil, water bottle, rope) to their correct unit (L, g, cm).

activities.differentiation: Use rulers with high-contrast markings for students with visual impairments.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student can verbally explain the importance of starting at the zero mark.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins demonstration, 20 mins guided practice measuring a single object together, 10 mins Q&A.
activities.safety: Ensure rulers have rounded edges to prevent poking injuries.
activities.task: Demonstrate how to align the zero mark of a ruler with the edge of an object and read the measurement in centimeters.

activities.differentiation: Provide objects with flat, rigid edges to make alignment easier for students developing fine motor skills.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student records measurements that are within +/- 0.5 cm of the actual length.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instruction, 40 mins active measuring in pairs, 10 mins sharing results.
activities.safety: Clear aisles so students can move safely around the classroom while measuring.
activities.task: Students work in pairs to measure and record the length of 5 specific classroom objects (e.g., desk edge, book, pencil) in centimeters.

activities.differentiation: Provide a ruler with a physical stop at the zero mark for students with severe motor tremors, maintaining the cognitive task of reading the number.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student measures both objects accurately to the nearest centimeter (+/- 0.5 cm).
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins setup, 25 mins independent measurement, 10 mins collection.
activities.task: Students independently measure the length of a provided sticky note and a pencil using a ruler, recording their answers in centimeters.

activities.differentiation: Provide a graphic organizer comparing the two scales' purposes for students who need visual structuring of information.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student can articulate that different scales have different sensitivities.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins introduction, 25 mins demonstration and observation, 20 mins guided discussion on sensitivity.
activities.safety: Clean up any spilled salt immediately to prevent slipping.
activities.task: Show a bathroom scale and a kitchen scale. Place a spoonful of salt on both to demonstrate that the bathroom scale does not register the small mass.

activities.differentiation: Allow students to verbally justify their choices instead of writing them down if they struggle with writing stamina.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly sorts items and provides a valid reason based on the object's mass.
materials: Sorting mats labeled 'Kitchen Scale' and 'Large Scale'
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instructions, 35 mins sorting and discussing in groups, 15 mins class review.
activities.safety: Ensure cards are laminated with rounded corners to prevent paper cuts.
activities.task: Students are given cards with pictures of various items (e.g., a single coffee bean, a sack of basic grains like beans or rice) and must sort them by which scale is appropriate, justifying their choice.

activities.differentiation: Provide sentence starters (e.g., 'I would use the ___ scale because...') for students needing language support.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student selects kitchen scale and states the bathroom scale is not sensitive enough for small masses.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instruction, 40 mins independent writing, 10 mins collection.
activities.task: Students write a short paragraph choosing whether to use a bathroom scale or a kitchen scale to measure a spoonful of salt, explaining their reasoning.

activities.differentiation: Use a digital simulation of a broken ruler for students who might struggle to handle the physical broken tool safely.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student can explain why the broken ruler gives a false reading.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins demonstration, 20 mins guided comparison of intact vs broken, 10 mins discussion.
activities.safety: Ensure the broken ends of the rulers are sanded smooth or taped to prevent injury.
activities.task: Present a ruler with the first 2 cm snapped off. Demonstrate how measuring a 5 cm object with it gives an incorrect reading if not adjusted, explaining reliability.

activities.differentiation: Limit the toolkit to 3 highly contrasting items for students who get overwhelmed by too many choices.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly identifies damaged tools as unreliable and links the damage to inaccurate readings.
materials: Toolkits with intact and damaged measuring tools
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instruction, 35 mins inspection and logging, 15 mins sharing findings.
activities.safety: Ensure all damaged tools are safe to handle (no sharp edges, no exposed springs).
activities.task: Students inspect a 'toolkit' of various measuring devices (some intact, some intentionally damaged like a stretched measuring tape) and categorize them as reliable or unreliable, writing a reason for each.

activities.differentiation: Allow oral responses recorded by the teacher for students with severe dysgraphia.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student states it is unreliable and links the missing starting point to incorrect measurements.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instruction, 25 mins independent writing, 10 mins collection.
activities.task: Students look at a picture of a ruler missing the zero mark and write whether it is reliable for measuring, explaining why.

activities.differentiation: Provide a word bank (e.g., accurate, missing, reliable) to support vocabulary retrieval.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student identifies it as unreliable because the missing part prevents accurate mass measurement.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 mins presentation, 15 mins writing, 10 mins peer review.
activities.task: Quick recall: Show an image of a kitchen scale with a missing weighing pan. Ask students to write down if it is reliable and why.

activities.differentiation: Have students physically mimic the push and pull motions with their hands while observing, aiding kinesthetic learners.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student can define a force as a push or a pull that changes motion.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins demonstration, 20 mins interactive discussion, 10 mins summarizing.
activities.safety: Ensure the toy car is large enough not to be a tripping hazard and has no sharp edges.
activities.task: Introduce forces as pushes and pulls using a toy car. Demonstrate pushing to start, pulling to move closer, and pushing/pulling to stop the car.

activities.differentiation: Provide visual cue cards (arrows pointing away for push, towards for pull) for students to hold up instead of shouting out.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly identifies the force in at least 4 out of 5 acted scenarios.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instruction, 40 mins acting and identifying, 10 mins review.
activities.safety: Ensure clear space for acting out scenarios to prevent collisions.
activities.task: Students act out various scenarios (e.g., opening a door, pressing a button, tug-of-war) and the class identifies the primary force as a push or pull.

activities.differentiation: Include simple illustrations next to the text descriptions for students with lower reading comprehension.
