activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly classifies at least 4 out of 5 actions.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instruction, 25 mins independent work, 10 mins collection.
activities.task: Students classify a written list of 5 actions (kicking a ball, stopping a rolling ball, pressing a doorbell, pulling a wagon, closing a drawer) as a push or a pull.

activities.differentiation: Allow students to touch the smooth table and the rough carpet to physically feel the difference in surfaces causing friction.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student can state that friction opposes motion and makes objects stop faster on rougher surfaces.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins demonstration, 25 mins guided discussion on why the book stops, 20 mins concept mapping.
activities.safety: Ensure the carpet square has a non-slip backing so it doesn't slide off the table.
activities.task: Slide a book across a smooth table and then across a piece of carpet. Ask students to predict and observe the difference. Explicitly teach that friction is the force opposing the motion, causing it to stop faster on rough surfaces.

activities.differentiation: Pre-mark the measuring tapes with color codes for students who struggle with reading large numbers, focusing them on the concept of distance related to friction.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student identifies that rougher surfaces apply more friction, stopping the car sooner.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins setup and instruction, 30 mins experiment and data collection, 15 mins conclusion sharing.
activities.safety: Tape down the sandpaper and towels to prevent slipping hazards on the floor.
activities.task: Students roll toy cars down a ramp onto different surfaces (tile, towel, sandpaper) and measure how far they go, identifying friction as the stopping force.

activities.differentiation: Provide a fill-in-the-blank version (e.g., 'The car stops faster on sandpaper because of a force called ____ which acts ____ the movement.') for students needing scaffolding.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student predicts sandpaper and explicitly names friction as the opposing force.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instruction, 40 mins independent writing, 10 mins collection.
activities.task: Students read a scenario about a toy car rolling on glass versus sandpaper, predict which surface stops it faster, and write an explanation using the concept of friction.

activities.differentiation: Use smaller, desk-sized boxes (empty vs filled with coins) for students to push with their fingers if they need a localized, seated demonstration.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student can explain that objects with more mass require more force to move.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins demonstration, 25 mins guided discussion linking mass to force, 20 mins summarizing.
activities.safety: Teacher performs the heavy lifting/pushing to prevent student strain; ensure boxes are pushed in a clear area.
activities.task: Demonstrate pushing an empty cardboard box versus a box filled with heavy books across the floor. Introduce the dynamometer as a tool to measure the force applied. Discuss why the heavier box requires more effort.

activities.differentiation: Provide pre-drawn charts for recording stretch length to help students organize their data easily.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student concludes that the rubber band stretches more (more force) for the object with more mass.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins instruction and safety briefing, 30 mins experiment, 15 mins class discussion.
activities.safety: Require safety goggles to protect eyes in case a rubber band snaps.
activities.task: Students use a rubber band or a simple dynamometer to pull different objects (a wooden block, a block with weights) and observe the force required, relating it to mass.

activities.differentiation: Allow students to draw a diagram with force arrows to supplement their written explanation.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student selects the heavier box and explicitly links the required force to the object's mass.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instruction, 40 mins independent work, 10 mins collection.
activities.task: Students read a scenario about an empty box and a box full of books, predict which requires more force to push, and explain why.

activities.differentiation: Use a document camera to project the demonstration on a large screen for students with visual impairments.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student can point out the poles as the areas with the most iron filings.
materials: Iron filings in a sealed case or shaker
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 20 mins demonstration, 20 mins guided observation of the pattern, 20 mins discussion on poles.
activities.safety: Use a sealed iron filing case for the teacher demonstration or project via a document camera to ensure no loose filings are present in the classroom environment.
activities.task: Demonstrate placing a piece of paper over a bar magnet and sprinkling iron filings to reveal the magnetic field lines, explaining the concentration at the poles.

activities.differentiation: Provide a faint outline of a bar magnet on the drawing paper to help students orient their drawings.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student draws a pattern showing lines connecting poles and clustering at the ends.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instruction, 35 mins observation and drawing, 15 mins sharing drawings.
activities.safety: Use sealed cases for iron filings to completely eliminate the risk of inhalation or eye irritation.
activities.task: Students work in small groups with sealed plastic cases containing iron filings and a magnet. They place the magnet under the case, observe the pattern, and practice drawing it.

activities.differentiation: Allow students to use a reference photo of a real magnetic field for 30 seconds before drawing from memory, if they struggle with visual recall.
activities.mastery_criterion: Drawing shows distinct poles where filings cluster and lines connecting them.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instruction, 40 mins independent drawing, 10 mins collection.
activities.task: Students are given a blank outline of a magnet and must draw the pattern of iron filings they would expect to see, highlighting the poles.

activities.differentiation: Use a slow-falling object like a feather alongside a fast one to show gravity acts on both, aiding visual processing.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student can define gravity as a downward pull from the Earth.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins demonstration, 20 mins direct instruction on the concept of gravity, 10 mins Q&A.
activities.safety: Ensure dropped objects are soft or light to prevent injury to feet or damage to the floor.
activities.task: Drop various objects (a ball, a crumpled paper, a pencil) to demonstrate that they all fall downwards. Explicitly teach that gravity is the Earth's downward pull.

activities.differentiation: Provide cards with clear, unambiguous downward motion arrows for students needing visual support.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly identifies scenarios where gravity is the primary force causing the observed motion.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instruction, 35 mins sorting in groups, 15 mins class review.
activities.task: Students sort picture cards of different scenarios (e.g., an apple falling, a magnet picking up a clip, a person pushing a cart) to identify which ones primarily show gravity acting.

activities.differentiation: Allow oral responses for students who struggle with writing.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student identifies gravity and states its downward direction.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instruction, 25 mins independent writing, 10 mins collection.
activities.task: Students answer the question: 'What force causes a dropped pencil to fall to the ground instead of floating?' in writing.

activities.differentiation: Provide a graphic organizer with the word 'Earth' in the center for students who need help structuring their thoughts.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student mentions gravity and the Earth pulling objects down.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 mins instruction, 15 mins writing, 10 mins sharing.
activities.task: Quick write: Students have 5 minutes to write everything they remember about why things fall when dropped.

activities.differentiation: Use a larger, wider object like a hardcover book for the demonstration to make the balance point more obvious.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student can state that equilibrium means forces and torque are balanced and cancel each other out.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins demonstration, 25 mins direct instruction on balanced forces and torque, 20 mins guided Q&A.
activities.safety: Ensure rulers are plastic or wood without sharp edges.
activities.task: Demonstrate balancing a ruler on a fulcrum. Explain that gravity pulls down, but the fulcrum pushes up, and introduce torque as the rotational force that must be balanced for rotational equilibrium.

activities.differentiation: Mark the exact center of the ruler with tape to help students find the initial balance point more easily.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student successfully balances the ruler and identifies the downward/upward forces and balanced torque acting on it.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins setup, 35 mins balancing activity and drawing, 15 mins discussion.
activities.safety: Ensure weights are not small enough to be a choking hazard.
activities.task: Students work to balance a ruler on a fulcrum (a marker) and place small identical weights on both sides to maintain rotational equilibrium, discussing how torque is balanced.

activities.differentiation: Provide a diagram of a balanced ruler and ask students to draw arrows representing the forces instead of writing a full paragraph.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student states that forces and torque are acting and that they cancel each other out to create equilibrium.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instruction, 40 mins independent balancing and writing, 10 mins collection.
activities.task: Students are asked to balance a ruler on a fulcrum and write an explanation of how the forces and torque create rotational equilibrium.

activities.differentiation: Provide a word bank of the units for students who need spelling support.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly identifies the unit for at least 8 out of 10 items.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 mins setup, 15 mins quick write, 10 mins peer grading and review.
activities.task: Students quickly write down the correct unit (g, L, cm) for a series of 10 household items displayed on the board.

activities.differentiation: Use thicker lines for students with visual impairments.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student measures all 3 lines accurately within +/- 0.5 cm.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 mins distribution, 15 mins measuring, 10 mins review.
activities.task: Students are given 3 pre-drawn lines on a paper and must quickly measure and record their lengths in centimeters.

activities.differentiation: Include pictures on the response cards for visual learners.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student holds up the correct card for at least 8 out of 10 objects.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 mins setup, 20 mins activity, 5 mins wrap-up.
activities.task: Teacher calls out an object (e.g., a feather, a person, a bag of rice) and students hold up a card indicating 'Kitchen Scale' or 'Bathroom Scale'.

activities.differentiation: Pause the video after each clip to allow extra processing time.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly identifies the force in all 5 video clips.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 mins setup, 15 mins viewing and writing, 10 mins review.
activities.task: Students view short video clips of everyday actions and write down whether each action is a push or a pull.

activities.differentiation: Provide a word bank for students who need vocabulary support.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly fills in 'friction' and 'opposes' (or similar terms).
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 mins distribution, 15 mins writing, 10 mins review.
activities.task: Students complete a quick fill-in-the-blank paragraph about why a rolling ball eventually stops on grass.

activities.differentiation: Allow students to verbally explain their choice if they point incorrectly.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly identifies the heavier object in all pairs.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 mins setup, 20 mins activity, 5 mins wrap-up.
activities.task: Students are shown pairs of objects (e.g., empty backpack vs full backpack) and must quickly point to the one that requires more force to lift.

activities.differentiation: Provide a partially drawn template on the whiteboard for students who need a starting point.
activities.mastery_criterion: Sketch shows lines connecting poles and clustering at the ends.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 mins instruction, 15 mins drawing, 10 mins review.
activities.task: Students sketch a magnetic field from memory on a mini-whiteboard and hold it up for the teacher to check.

activities.differentiation: Provide pre-drawn arrows that students only need to label.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student draws equal and opposite arrows for gravity (down) and the table's push (up).
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 mins distribution, 15 mins drawing, 10 mins review.
activities.task: Students look at a diagram of a book resting on a table and draw arrows to represent the balanced forces acting on it.

activities.differentiation: Provide large, clear images of thermometer scales for visually impaired students.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student can identify a thermometer and state its purpose.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins introduction, 20 mins showing different types, 10 mins discussion.
activities.safety: Ensure glass thermometers are handled only by the teacher.
activities.task: Introduce the thermometer as an instrument for measuring temperature. Show different types (clinical, environmental) and discuss their uses.

activities.differentiation: Read scenarios aloud for students with reading difficulties.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly matches 4 out of 5 scenarios.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instruction, 25 mins matching activity, 10 mins review.
activities.task: Students match different scenarios (e.g., checking for a fever, checking the weather) to the correct type of thermometer.

activities.differentiation: Allow oral responses for students with writing difficulties.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student identifies the thermometer and mentions temperature.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instruction, 25 mins independent work, 10 mins collection.
activities.task: Students answer a written question identifying the instrument used to measure body temperature and its unit.

activities.differentiation: Use a slow-motion video of a thrown ball to help students see the trajectory clearly.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student can describe the two directions of movement in projectile motion.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins demonstration, 20 mins discussion, 10 mins summarizing.
activities.safety: Ensure the area is clear of breakable objects.
activities.task: Demonstrate projectile motion by tossing a ball into a bin. Discuss how the ball moves forward and up/down at the same time.

activities.differentiation: Provide pre-drawn axes for students to plot the trajectory.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student draws a curved trajectory and labels the forward and vertical motions.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 20 mins building catapults, 25 mins launching and observing, 15 mins drawing.
activities.safety: Ensure students only launch soft objects (cotton balls) and aim away from faces.
activities.task: Students build a simple popsicle stick catapult and launch a small plastic spoon or cotton ball, observing and drawing the curved path (projectile motion).

activities.differentiation: Provide a word bank (e.g., forward, upward, downward, projectile).
activities.mastery_criterion: Student identifies projectile motion and mentions forward and vertical movement.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instruction, 25 mins independent writing, 10 mins collection.
activities.task: Students look at a picture of a basketball being thrown toward a hoop and describe the type of motion and the directions it is moving.

activities.differentiation: Provide visual cue cards showing 'new stuff made' for chemical and 'same stuff' for physical.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly identify tearing as physical and mixing as chemical, citing the formation of bubbles as evidence of a new substance.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins introduction, 15 mins demonstration, 15 mins guided discussion and classification.
activities.safety: Teacher handles vinegar and baking soda. Students observe from a safe distance. Goggles worn by teacher.
activities.task: Observe teacher tear paper and mix baking soda with vinegar. Discuss and classify each change as physical or chemical based on whether a new substance is formed.

activities.differentiation: Pair students for collaborative reading of station instructions.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly classify melting and dissolving as physical, and rusting as chemical.
materials: pre-rusted steel wool in sealed jars
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins setup and instructions, 45 mins station rotation (15 mins each), 15 mins wrap-up.
activities.safety: Steel wool is sealed in jars to prevent handling of sharp or rusty edges. Spills wiped immediately.
activities.task: Rotate through stations observing safe changes: melting ice, dissolving sugar in water, and observing pre-rusted steel wool. Classify each change on a recording sheet.

activities.differentiation: Provide a reference sheet with definitions and one example of each change type.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students accurately sort at least 8 out of 10 cards into the correct categories.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins review, 45 mins sorting activity and peer checking, 15 mins whole-class review.
activities.safety: Standard classroom safety. No hazardous materials used.
activities.task: Sort picture cards of everyday scenarios (e.g., baking bread, cutting wood, rotting fruit, molding clay) into physical and chemical change categories.

activities.differentiation: Read the descriptions aloud for students with reading difficulties.
activities.mastery_criterion: Correctly recalls the classifications of the taught examples; this is not evidence of transfer to a novel case.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instructions, 25 mins independent work, 10 mins collection and transition.
activities.task: Read descriptions of three events: baking bread, tearing paper, and rusting metal. Write down whether each is a physical or chemical change.

activities.differentiation: Use simple terms like 'can go back' and 'cannot go back'.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students state that melting is reversible because water can be frozen again, while cutting an apple is irreversible.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins demonstration, 20 mins discussion on the concept of reversibility.
activities.safety: Teacher uses the knife. Students observe only.
activities.task: Observe the teacher melt an ice cube and then show a pre-frozen ice cube. Then observe the teacher cut an apple. Discuss which change can be undone.

activities.differentiation: Provide pre-folded lines for students struggling with fine motor skills.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students categorize folding as reversible and cutting as irreversible.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instructions, 35 mins hands-on activity, 15 mins sharing conclusions.
activities.task: Students test folding a piece of paper into an origami shape versus cutting a piece of paper into pieces. They categorize each action.

activities.differentiation: Provide pre-cut images for groups that need more time focusing on categorization rather than cutting.
activities.mastery_criterion: Posters contain at least three correct examples in each column.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins planning, 40 mins poster creation, 10 mins gallery walk.
activities.safety: Standard classroom safety with scissors and glue.
activities.task: Create a group poster with two columns: Reversible and Irreversible. Draw or paste examples of changes in the correct columns.

activities.differentiation: Allow oral responses for students who struggle with writing.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly identify melted ice as reversible, and the broken cup and burned paper as irreversible.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instructions, 25 mins independent work, 10 mins collection.
activities.task: Categorize images of a broken cup, melted ice, and burned paper as reversible or irreversible on a worksheet.

activities.differentiation: Provide a visual chart matching the block models to the definitions.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students can verbally define simple and compound substances based on the block models.
materials: interlocking plastic blocks in various colors
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins modeling with blocks, 15 mins guided practice identifying teacher-made models.
activities.safety: Ensure blocks are large enough to not be a choking hazard.
activities.task: Use colored interlocking blocks to demonstrate simple substances (all blocks same color) and compound substances (blocks of different colors joined together).

activities.differentiation: Pre-roll clay balls for students with motor difficulties.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students build at least one model of a simple substance (one color) and one compound substance (multiple colors joined).
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instructions, 40 mins building and labeling, 10 mins cleanup.
activities.safety: Remind students clay is not for eating. Wash hands after use.
activities.task: Students use different colors of modeling clay to build their own models of simple and compound substances, labeling them on a mat.

activities.differentiation: Provide templates with outlines of particles for students to color in.
activities.mastery_criterion: Drawings accurately reflect single-type particles for simple substances and multi-type particles for compounds.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins review, 35 mins drawing, 10 mins peer sharing.
activities.task: Draw particle diagrams representing simple and compound substances based on written prompts.

activities.differentiation: Provide sentence starters for the definitions.
activities.mastery_criterion: Correctly defines simple (same particles) and compound (different particles) and draws matching diagrams.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instructions, 35 mins independent assessment.
activities.task: Write the definitions of simple and compound substances and provide a drawn example of each using circles to represent particles.

activities.differentiation: Use the terms 'looks like one thing' and 'can see different parts' alongside the formal vocabulary.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly identify the colored water as homogeneous and the sandy water as heterogeneous.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins demonstration, 20 mins discussion and observation, 10 mins vocabulary introduction.
activities.safety: Wipe up spills immediately to prevent slipping. Do not drink the mixtures.
activities.task: Mix water with food coloring in one clear cup, and water with sand in another. Discuss which mixture looks the same throughout and which does not.

activities.differentiation: Provide a checklist of steps for creating each mixture.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly classify water/salt and water/sugar as homogeneous, and water/oil and rice/beans as heterogeneous.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins setup, 45 mins mixing and classifying, 15 mins cleanup and review.
activities.safety: Ensure no students have allergies to the food items used. Do not consume.
activities.task: Students work in groups to create four safe mixtures (water/salt, water/oil, rice/beans, water/sugar) and classify them on a chart.

activities.differentiation: Group students to discuss the photographs before writing individual answers.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly classify at least 80% of the photographs.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins instructions, 45 mins analysis and classification, 15 mins whole-class review.
activities.task: Analyze photographs of everyday items (e.g., milk, a salad, concrete, clear apple juice) and classify them as homogeneous or heterogeneous.

activities.differentiation: Allow students to verbally explain their reasoning if writing is a barrier.
activities.mastery_criterion: Correctly classifies colored water as homogeneous (looks uniform) and pebble water as heterogeneous (can see parts).
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins observation, 35 mins writing explanations.
activities.safety: Jars are sealed to prevent spills.
activities.task: Observe two sealed jars provided by the teacher (one with colored water, one with water and pebbles). Write down the classification for each and explain why.

activities.differentiation: Provide a property chart (e.g., magnetic: yes/no, size: big/small) to help guide reasoning.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students can state that the magnet was used because clips are magnetic, and the filter was used because sand particles are larger than water particles.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 20 mins demonstrations, 40 mins guided discussion on properties and tool selection.
activities.safety: Ensure magnets are not swallowed. Handle iron clips carefully to avoid skin pinches.
activities.task: Demonstrate using a magnet to separate iron clips from sand, and a paper filter to separate sand from water. Discuss why each tool was chosen based on material properties.

activities.differentiation: Provide a graphic organizer for planning the steps before executing them.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students successfully separate the mixture using a magnet first, then a sieve, justifying choices based on magnetism and size.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins planning, 45 mins execution and justification writing, 15 mins cleanup.
activities.safety: Goggles worn to prevent dust in eyes. Wash hands after handling materials.
activities.task: Provide groups with a mixture of gravel, sand, and iron clips. Students must select tools and sequence their actions to separate all three components, justifying their choices.

activities.differentiation: Provide a word bank of separation tools and material properties.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students select a magnet for caps, a sieve or hand-picking for leaves, and a filter for dirt, justifying based on properties.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins scenario introduction, 45 mins planning and writing, 15 mins sharing plans.
activities.task: Design a theoretical plan to clean a sample of dirty water containing leaves, dirt, and metal bottle caps. Select separation methods and justify them.

activities.differentiation: Provide sentence frames for the justification section.
activities.mastery_criterion: Selects a sieve and justifies the choice by stating that salt particles are much smaller than beans.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instructions, 35 mins independent writing.
activities.task: Given a written scenario of a mixture of dry beans and salt, select a separation method and write a justification based on the properties of the materials.

activities.differentiation: Allow students to consult a peer before raising their card.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students quickly and accurately select the correct tool and state the relevant physical property.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 mins setup, 25 mins gameplay and rapid review.
activities.task: Flashcard game: Teacher shows a mixture (e.g., water and pebbles), students hold up a card showing the best separation tool (filter, magnet, sieve) and explain why.

activities.differentiation: Limit the tool choices to just two (sieve or magnet) for students needing simplified options.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students select the sieve, justifying that size is the differing property, and successfully separate the beads.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 mins instructions, 15 mins separation task, 10 mins cleanup and verbal justification.
activities.safety: Ensure beads are not put in mouths.
activities.task: Quick lab: Students are given a mixture of large wooden beads and small plastic beads. They must choose between a magnet, a sieve, or a filter to separate them and do it.

activities.differentiation: Provide a visual anchor chart with the three rock types and their key features.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students can point to the correct rock type when the teacher describes a key feature (e.g., 'has fossils' -> sedimentary).
materials: rock samples (pumice, sandstone, slate) or high-res images
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 20 mins introduction of types, 25 mins guided observation of samples.
activities.safety: Instruct students not to throw or drop rocks. Wash hands after handling.
activities.task: Introduce igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic rocks using large physical samples or high-quality images. Highlight key observable features (crystals, layers/fossils, banding).

activities.differentiation: Provide a checklist of features to look for at each station.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly classify at least 4 out of 6 rocks based on observable features like layers, crystals, or banding.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins instructions and safety, 45 mins station rotation, 15 mins whole-class review.
activities.safety: Rocks must remain on the table. No throwing.
activities.task: Rock observation stations. Students use hand lenses to observe 6 different unidentified rock samples, note their features, and classify them into the three types.

activities.differentiation: Include small icons on the description cards to aid reading comprehension.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly match all descriptions to igneous, sedimentary, or metamorphic categories.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins review, 45 mins sorting activity in pairs, 15 mins checking answers.
activities.task: Match written descriptions of rock formation and features (e.g., 'cooled quickly from lava', 'squished deep underground') to the correct rock type category on a large sorting mat.

activities.differentiation: Read the descriptions aloud for the class.
activities.mastery_criterion: Correctly classifies the shell rock as sedimentary, lava rock as igneous, and deformed rock as metamorphic.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instructions, 35 mins independent work.
activities.task: Read descriptions of three rocks (one with shells, one from cooled lava, one deformed by heat/pressure). Classify each as igneous, sedimentary, or metamorphic.

activities.differentiation: Use hand gestures to represent each process (e.g., rubbing hands for weathering, pressing hands for deformation).
activities.mastery_criterion: Students can verbally repeat the sequence of processes that turn a surface rock into magma.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 25 mins direct instruction with diagram, 20 mins guided sequencing practice on the board.
activities.task: Introduce the rock cycle using a large wall diagram. Explain weathering, erosion, deformation, and melting as the processes that move rocks through the cycle.

activities.differentiation: Provide pre-shaved crayons for students with fine motor difficulties.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly label their observation sheets with the corresponding rock cycle processes for each crayon stage.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins instructions, 45 mins simulation and recording, 15 mins cleanup and review.
activities.safety: Teacher handles all hot water and melting. Students use safe plastic knives for shaving. Goggles worn.
activities.task: Crayon rock cycle simulation. Students shave crayons (weathering), press shavings (sedimentary), and observe teacher melt them in hot water (magma/igneous).

activities.differentiation: Provide a template with the first and last panels already drawn.
activities.mastery_criterion: The storyboard correctly sequences the processes in a logical loop including weathering, sedimentation, deformation, and melting.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins planning, 45 mins drawing and writing, 15 mins sharing stories.
activities.task: Create a comic strip storyboard showing the full journey of a rock: weathering into sediment, pressing into sedimentary rock, deforming under heat/pressure into metamorphic rock, and melting into magma.

activities.differentiation: Provide a simplified diagram of the Earth's layers as a hint for where melting occurs.
activities.mastery_criterion: Cards are glued in the correct logical sequence: Weathering -> Erosion -> Deformation -> Melting.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instructions, 35 mins independent sequencing and gluing.
activities.task: Given cards with the terms weathering, erosion, deformation, and melting, sequence them to show the order of processes that transform a surface rock into magma, and glue them on paper.

activities.differentiation: Use clear visual diagrams comparing the syrup pile to a stratovolcano and the water puddle to a shield volcano.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students can explain that fluid lava creates wide, flat shapes (shield) and thick lava creates steep shapes (stratovolcano).
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 20 mins demonstration, 40 mins discussion and connecting models to real volcano types.
activities.safety: Wipe spills immediately. Do not consume the syrup.
activities.task: Pour water (fluid lava model) and thick syrup (viscous lava model) onto a flat tray. Observe how they spread or pile up. Discuss how this relates to volcano shapes.

activities.differentiation: Highlight key words in the descriptions like 'runny', 'spreads far', 'thick', 'explodes'.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students build a wide, flat model for the effusive description and a steep, cone model for the explosive description.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins reading descriptions, 45 mins building models, 15 mins gallery walk.
activities.task: Students read descriptions of two historical eruptions (one effusive, one explosive) and build clay models of the predicted volcano shapes.

activities.differentiation: Provide a sentence starter: 'I predict this is a [shape] volcano because the eruption is [effusive/explosive], which means it will [spread/pile up].'
activities.mastery_criterion: Correctly predicts structures based on eruption images and justifies using the relationship between eruption type and shape.
materials: images of eruptions from the text
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins image reading instruction, 45 mins analysis and writing, 15 mins review.
activities.task: Analyze images of different volcanic eruptions (effusive and explosive) from the provided text. Predict the resulting volcano structure for each and justify based on the eruption type.

activities.differentiation: Allow students to draw their prediction alongside their written justification.
activities.mastery_criterion: Predicts stratovolcano and justifies that thick lava and ash pile up steeply rather than spreading out.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instructions, 35 mins independent writing.
activities.task: Read data about a volcano that historically erupted with thick, slow-moving lava and large ash clouds. Predict its shape (shield or stratovolcano) and write a justification.

activities.differentiation: Reduce the number of cards for students who need a more focused review.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly match fluid/few gases to shield, and thick/lots of gas to stratovolcano.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 mins instructions, 20 mins matching gameplay, 5 mins review.
activities.task: Matching game: Students match cards describing lava properties (fluid, thick, lots of gas, few gases) to cards showing volcano shapes (shield, stratovolcano).

activities.differentiation: Provide verbal reminders of the definitions of fluid and viscous before reading the prompts.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students consistently draw wide shapes for fluid lava prompts and steep shapes for thick lava prompts.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 mins setup, 25 mins rapid drawing and feedback rounds.
activities.task: Quick draw: Teacher reads an eruption scenario. Students have 2 minutes to draw the resulting volcano shape on a whiteboard and hold it up.

activities.differentiation: Provide a labeled diagram of the egg model next to a diagram of the Earth.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students can name the three compositional layers and state that physical properties like density differences keep them from mixing.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins demonstration, 30 mins discussion and diagram labeling.
activities.safety: Teacher cuts the egg. Check for egg allergies before bringing them into the classroom. Do not eat the models.
activities.task: Cut a hard-boiled egg in half to model the Earth's compositional layers (shell=crust, white=mantle, yolk=core). Explain that real layers separate due to different physical properties like density, distinguishing between the names of the layers and the reason they separate.

activities.differentiation: Provide pre-cut circles of different sizes for students to assemble.
activities.mastery_criterion: Collage includes compositional layers and the lithosphere in correct order, labeled, with a sentence mentioning density or physical properties preventing mixing.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins instructions, 45 mins creating collages, 15 mins sharing.
activities.task: Create a scale drawing or colored paper collage of the Earth's layers, labeling the compositional layers (crust, mantle, core) and the physical layers (lithosphere as the hard outer shell), and writing a sentence about why they don't mix.

activities.differentiation: Provide a fill-in-the-blank paragraph connecting the liquid column to the Earth's layers.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students draw the column, label the liquids, and write a comparison to the Earth's layers separating by density, noting it does not represent liquid/solid states.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 20 mins demonstration, 40 mins drawing and writing comparisons, 15 mins review.
activities.safety: Teacher handles the liquids. Wipe spills immediately. Do not drink.
activities.task: Observe a density column demonstration (oil, water, syrup). Discuss how this models how layers separate by density, not their state of matter. Teacher note: Emphasize that the mantle is mostly solid but behaves like a thick fluid over time. Students draw and label the column.

activities.differentiation: Provide a word bank for the layer names.
activities.mastery_criterion: Correctly labels all three layers in order (outside to inside) and states that they have different densities/physical properties.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instructions, 35 mins independent assessment.
activities.task: Label a blank diagram of the Earth's interior with crust, mantle, and core. Write one sentence explaining why these layers do not mix together.

activities.differentiation: Use a simple graphic organizer showing 'Fire needs -> Oxygen' and 'Humans need -> Oxygen'.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students articulate that the candle went out because it used up the oxygen, and connect this to human need for atmospheric oxygen.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins demonstration, 30 mins guided discussion on the importance of the atmosphere.
activities.safety: Teacher only demonstration. Conducted on a fireproof tray away from flammable materials. Fire extinguisher nearby.
activities.task: Teacher lights a small candle and covers it with a glass jar. Students observe it go out. Discuss that fire needs oxygen from the air, just like humans do.

activities.differentiation: Provide a structured outline for the paragraph (Topic sentence, Evidence, Conclusion).
activities.mastery_criterion: Paragraph justifies the spacesuit by stating the Moon lacks an atmosphere with oxygen, which humans need to survive.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins scenario reading, 45 mins writing, 15 mins peer review.
activities.task: Analyze a scenario of an astronaut on the Moon versus a person on Earth. Write a paragraph justifying why the astronaut needs a spacesuit using knowledge of the atmosphere.

activities.differentiation: Discuss the photos in small groups before requiring independent writing.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students justify that the sealed plant died because it ran out of necessary gases from the atmosphere, showing the atmosphere's importance for life.
materials: photo sets of the plant experiment
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins photo observation, 45 mins group discussion and writing, 15 mins whole-class summary.
activities.task: Review time-lapse photos of a plant in a sealed jar versus an open jar. Discuss and write about why the sealed plant died, relating it to atmospheric gases.

activities.differentiation: Allow students to draw a diagram to support their written explanation.
activities.mastery_criterion: Explains that exhaust gases displace oxygen, and justifies that humans require the oxygen in the atmosphere to breathe and live.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instructions, 35 mins independent writing.
activities.task: Explain in writing why a town in a valley with poor air circulation and a buildup of exhaust gases is dangerous for residents, relating it to the human need for atmospheric oxygen.

activities.differentiation: Provide tactile graphics for visually impaired students.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student can verbally name at least three water bodies shown in the photographs.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes introduction, 20 minutes guided observation, 10 minutes summary.
activities.safety: Ensure photographs are clear and accessible to all students.
activities.task: Observe photographs of oceans, lakes, rivers, glaciers, and aquifers. Discuss the defining characteristics of each water body.

activities.differentiation: Reduce the number of categories to three for students needing simplified tasks.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly sorts at least 16 out of 20 cards into the proper categories.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes setup, 35 minutes sorting activity, 15 minutes peer review.
activities.safety: Use laminated cards with rounded corners.
activities.task: Sort a set of 20 picture cards into five categories: river, lake, ocean, glacier, aquifer.

activities.differentiation: Allow oral responses for students with writing difficulties.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly identifies at least 4 out of 5 water body types from visual representations.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instructions, 35 minutes independent assessment.
activities.task: Given a set of 5 photographs showing different water bodies, write the correct name under each.

activities.differentiation: Provide a word bank.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly matches all five definitions.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes recall prompt, 25 minutes matching, 10 minutes review.
activities.task: Match written definitions to the names of the five water bodies without looking at notes.

activities.differentiation: Provide a pre-drawn landscape where students only need to add labels.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student includes and correctly labels at least three of the requested water bodies.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instructions, 35 minutes drawing and labeling.
activities.task: Draw a landscape that includes a river, a lake, an ocean, and a glacier, labeling each one.

activities.differentiation: Use physical blocks (97 blue, 3 green) for tactile learners.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student can state that most of Earths water is salt water.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes explanation, 20 minutes interactive demonstration, 10 minutes summary.
activities.task: Introduce the concept of Earths water distribution using a 100-part grid to represent total water.

activities.differentiation: Provide grids with the 3 parts already outlined for students needing fine motor support.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student accurately colors 97 parts blue and 3 parts green for the Earth grid.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes setup, 40 minutes coloring and comparing, 10 minutes cleanup.
activities.task: Work in pairs to color multiple 100-part grids representing different hypothetical planets, then color Earths grid.

activities.differentiation: Allow students to use stamps instead of coloring if they have motor difficulties.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student colors exactly 97 parts for salt water and 3 parts for fresh water.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instructions, 35 minutes independent work.
activities.task: Using a 10x10 grid representing all the water on Earth, color the squares to show how much is salt water and how much is fresh water.

activities.differentiation: Provide a smaller, desktop version of the demonstration for closer observation.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student can explain that water moves from higher to lower ground.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes setup and intro, 20 minutes demonstration, 10 minutes discussion.
activities.safety: Wipe up any spilled water immediately to prevent slipping.
activities.task: Demonstrate how water flows downhill by pouring water over a slanted plastic board into a basin.

activities.differentiation: Provide pre-shaped clay landscapes for students with limited hand strength.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student successfully builds a channel that directs water into a lower basin.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes building, 30 minutes testing and observing, 15 minutes cleanup.
activities.safety: Ensure all water spills are cleaned immediately. Do not drink the water.
activities.task: In groups, build a landscape with clay on a tray, create a river channel, and test water flow with different amounts of poured water.

activities.differentiation: Allow oral description of the water level changes instead of written.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student builds a sloped channel leading to a basin and demonstrates increased flow when water is poured.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 25 minutes modeling, 20 minutes writing description.
activities.safety: Clean spills immediately to prevent slipping hazards.
activities.task: Using clay and a tray, build a model of a river flowing into a lake. Pour water to simulate rain and describe what happens to the river level.

activities.differentiation: Use a 3D sponge model to show absorption for visual learners.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student can point to the aquifer on the diagram and explain how water got there.
materials: Large diagram of soil layers and aquifer
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 20 minutes explanation, 15 minutes Q&A, 10 minutes summary.
activities.task: Show a diagram of soil layers and explain how rain soaks into the ground to form aquifers.

activities.differentiation: Number the backs of the cards for self-checking.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly sequences all four stages of infiltration.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instructions, 35 minutes sequencing practice, 15 minutes review.
activities.task: Sequence a set of cards showing rain falling, water on the surface, water moving through soil, and water in an aquifer.

activities.differentiation: Provide a partially drawn diagram where the student only adds arrows and labels.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student accurately sequences the movement of water from the surface through porous materials.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instructions, 35 minutes drawing and labeling.
activities.task: Draw a diagram showing what happens to rain after it falls on the ground, labeling the movement of water through the soil.

activities.differentiation: Use simple, highly contrasting images for visual clarity.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student can state two negative effects of lack of water on living things.
materials: Pictures of healthy and dried plants
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 20 minutes discussion on water needs, 25 minutes exploring drought images.
activities.task: Discuss the biological need for water in plants and animals, and introduce the concept of drought.

activities.differentiation: Read scenarios aloud for students with reading difficulties.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student writes logical predictions based on the biological need for water.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes reading, 30 minutes writing predictions, 15 minutes sharing.
activities.task: Read three short scenarios about different environments facing drought. Write a prediction for what will happen to the local wildlife in each.

activities.differentiation: Allow students to draw their predictions and explain them orally.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student justifies the negative impact of water scarcity on specific living organisms.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instructions, 35 minutes independent writing.
activities.task: Read the scenario about a region with no rain for 6 months. Predict what will happen to the local trees and birds, and justify your answer.

activities.differentiation: Use physical props (a toy well, a cup, a toy drain) to represent the stages.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student can verbally list the three main stages of human water use.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 20 minutes explanation, 25 minutes interactive flowchart building on the board.
activities.task: Explain the cycle of extracting water from the environment, using it in homes, and discharging wastewater.

activities.differentiation: Provide pre-printed labels for students to glue onto their posters.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student includes all three stages in the correct order on their poster.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes planning, 40 minutes creating posters, 10 minutes cleanup.
activities.task: Create a poster showing the stages of water extraction, human use, and wastewater discharge, using drawings and labels.

activities.differentiation: Provide a template with boxes indicating where cards should be glued.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly orders the stages of extraction, use, and return.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instructions, 35 minutes arranging and gluing.
activities.task: Arrange the provided cards (Extraction, Human use, Wastewater discharge) in the correct order and draw arrows between them.

activities.differentiation: Provide magnifying glasses to observe the sand particles that do not dissolve.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student can define soluble as dissolving in water and insoluble as not dissolving.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes demonstration, 20 minutes explanation of terms, 10 minutes summary.
activities.safety: Do not taste any of the mixtures. Clean up spills immediately.
activities.task: Demonstrate mixing salt in water (soluble) and sand in water (insoluble). Define the terms soluble and insoluble.

activities.differentiation: Provide a recording sheet with pictures of the substances.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly classifies at least three of the four powders.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes setup and safety briefing, 30 minutes testing, 15 minutes cleanup and review.
activities.safety: Do not taste any substances. Wear safety goggles to prevent powder in eyes.
activities.task: Test four safe household powders (sugar, flour, baking soda, coffee grounds) by mixing them in water and recording if they are soluble or insoluble.

activities.differentiation: Allow students to point to the soluble/insoluble mixtures and state their answers orally.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly categorizes at least 3 out of 4 tested substances.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes setup, 25 minutes testing and writing, 10 minutes cleanup.
activities.safety: Do not taste any substances. Wash hands after the assessment.
activities.task: Mix salt, sand, sugar, and soil into separate cups of water. Stir well. Write down which substances are soluble and which are insoluble.

activities.differentiation: Provide pictures next to the words on the list.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly sorts all four substances based on prior knowledge.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instructions, 25 minutes sorting, 10 minutes review.
activities.task: Sort a written list of known substances (salt, sand, sugar, soil) into two columns: Soluble and Insoluble, without testing them.

activities.differentiation: Read the log aloud to the student.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student identifies the powder as soluble based on the description.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes reading, 25 minutes answering questions, 10 minutes discussion.
activities.task: Read a short experiment log describing a powder that disappeared when stirred into water. Identify if the powder was soluble or insoluble.

activities.differentiation: Use a very dark color like blue or red for maximum contrast for visually impaired students.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student can state that more drops make the water a darker color.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes demonstration, 20 minutes discussion on concentration, 10 minutes summary.
activities.safety: Avoid getting food coloring on clothes or skin.
activities.task: Add 1, 3, and 6 drops of food coloring to three identical cups of water. Discuss how the color intensity relates to the amount of coloring added.

activities.differentiation: Provide sentence starters for the explanation.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly orders the cups and explains that more powder makes a darker color.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes setup, 30 minutes mixing and ordering, 15 minutes writing and cleanup.
activities.safety: Do not drink the solutions. Clean spills immediately.
activities.task: Create three solutions using 1, 2, and 4 spoons of colored drink mix. Order them by color intensity and write a sentence explaining the order.

activities.differentiation: Allow oral explanation of the reasoning.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly sequences solutions from least to most concentrated and justifies the order.
materials: Three pre-mixed cups of colored solution of varying concentration
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes observation, 35 minutes writing explanation.
activities.task: Look at the three cups of drink mix provided by the teacher. Order them from least concentrated to most concentrated. Explain how you know.

activities.differentiation: Provide a reference chart with pictures of the three types of mixtures.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student can name the three types of mixtures shown.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 20 minutes demonstration, 15 minutes explanation of terms, 10 minutes summary.
activities.safety: Do not shine the flashlight directly into eyes.
activities.task: Show a solution (saltwater), a colloid (milk in water), and a suspension (dirt in water). Shine a flashlight through each to show light scattering and settling.

activities.differentiation: Work in pairs so one student can hold the flashlight while the other records.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly classifies at least two of the three mystery cups.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes setup, 35 minutes observation and recording, 15 minutes cleanup and review.
activities.safety: Do not shine flashlights in eyes. Do not taste mixtures.
activities.task: Observe three mystery cups with a flashlight. Record if particles settle, if light scatters, or if it is clear. Classify each cup.

activities.differentiation: Read the descriptions aloud for students with reading difficulties.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student matches the type of dispersion to its observable characteristics.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instructions, 35 minutes independent matching.
activities.task: Match the terms (Solution, Colloid, Suspension) to their descriptions regarding settling and light scattering.

activities.differentiation: Use larger cups and more distinct layers (like gravel and water) for easier observation.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student can describe the steps of decantation verbally.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes demonstration, 20 minutes step-by-step breakdown, 10 minutes summary.
activities.safety: Clean up any spilled water immediately.
activities.task: Demonstrate how to separate sand and water by letting the sand settle and carefully pouring the water into a new cup.

activities.differentiation: Provide cups with pour spouts to assist with controlled pouring.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student successfully transfers mostly clear water while leaving the soil behind.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes mixing and waiting, 30 minutes decanting practice, 15 minutes cleanup.
activities.safety: Wash hands after handling soil. Clean spills immediately.
activities.task: Mix soil and water in a cup. Wait 10 minutes for it to settle, then practice decanting the water into an empty cup without moving the soil.

activities.differentiation: Allow students with motor difficulties to use a large syringe to extract the water instead of pouring, if pouring is physically impossible.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student successfully pours water leaving the majority of the sediment behind.
materials: Cups with pre-settled sand and water
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instructions, 25 minutes performing decantation, 10 minutes cleanup.
activities.task: Given a cup of water with settled sand, carefully pour the water into an empty cup without transferring the sand.

activities.differentiation: Use a large strainer with a cloth for a larger-scale, easier-to-see demonstration.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student can identify the cotton as the filter that catches the solid particles.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes setup demonstration, 20 minutes filtering observation, 10 minutes summary.
activities.safety: Do not drink the filtered water.
activities.task: Demonstrate setting up a funnel with cotton and pouring muddy water through it to separate the dirt from the water.

activities.differentiation: Pre-place the cotton in the funnel for students needing fine motor assistance.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student successfully sets up the filter and records that solids stay in the cotton.
materials: Water mixed with leaves and dirt
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes setup, 30 minutes filtering and recording, 15 minutes cleanup.
activities.safety: Do not drink the water. Wash hands after the activity.
activities.task: Set up a cotton filter in a funnel. Pour a mixture of water, leaves, and dirt through it. Observe and record the results.

activities.differentiation: Allow oral recording of observations.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student sets up a filter and successfully passes a mixture through it, trapping solids.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes setup, 25 minutes filtering and writing, 10 minutes cleanup.
activities.safety: Do not drink the water. Wash hands after the assessment.
activities.task: Set up a funnel with cotton. Pour a mixture of water and dirt through it. Observe and record what stays in the cotton and what passes through.

activities.differentiation: Provide a visual flowchart showing the two steps in order.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student can explain why decantation should happen before filtration.
materials: Diagram of a two-step cleaning process
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 20 minutes explanation, 15 minutes guided discussion, 10 minutes summary.
activities.task: Discuss how decantation and filtration can be combined to clean very dirty water, explaining why settling heavy items first makes filtering easier.

activities.differentiation: Provide a template with boxes for Step 1 and Step 2.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student includes both decantation and filtration in their written plan and diagram.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes group discussion, 35 minutes writing and drawing, 10 minutes sharing.
activities.task: Work in groups to write a plan to clean a specific sample of muddy water with twigs. Draw a diagram of the two-step process.

activities.differentiation: Allow students to draw their step-by-step plan instead of writing it.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student designs a logical sequence using both settling and filtering to improve water clarity.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instructions, 35 minutes independent writing.
activities.task: You have a bucket of muddy water with leaves and rocks. Write a step-by-step plan using decantation and filtration to make the water look clear.

activities.differentiation: Provide a pre-drawn outline of a plant for students who struggle with drawing, allowing them to focus on labeling.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly label the root system (below ground) and shoot system (above ground) with their respective organs.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins introduction, 30 mins observation and drawing, 15 mins labeling, 15 mins class review.
activities.safety: Ensure weeds are non-toxic and free of harmful pests. Students wash hands after handling.
activities.task: Students observe a complete uprooted weed (provided by the teacher), draw it, and label the shoot and root systems, listing the organs found in each.

activities.differentiation: Use visual icons (water drop, strong pillar) next to text to support vocabulary comprehension.
activities.mastery_criterion: Chart accurately lists water absorption for roots, water transport for stems, and support functions for both.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 20 mins observation, 30 mins chart creation, 25 mins discussion on functions.
activities.safety: Teacher pre-cuts the celery and carrots. No sharp tools for students.
activities.task: Students examine cross-sections of stems and roots using hand lenses, then create a two-column chart detailing the transport and support functions of each.

activities.differentiation: Read the sorting cards aloud for students with reading difficulties.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly sort 100% of the description cards into the transpiration or photosynthesis categories.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 25 mins diagram analysis, 30 mins sorting activity, 20 mins review and correction.
activities.task: Students review diagrams of a leaf showing water leaving (transpiration) and sunlight/air entering to make food (photosynthesis), then complete a sorting activity with cards describing each process.

activities.differentiation: Provide a partially completed sequence map with missing steps for students to fill in.
activities.mastery_criterion: Sequence map correctly shows the progression from flower to fruit to seed.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 30 mins dissection, 30 mins sequence mapping, 15 mins sharing.
activities.safety: Ensure no students have pollen allergies. Use plastic spoons instead of knives to open fruits.
activities.task: Students dissect a large flower (like a lily) and a soft fruit (like a tomato) to locate reproductive parts and seeds, recording their findings in a sequence map from flower to fruit.

activities.differentiation: Provide physical models or 3D prints of spores and cones for tactile learners.
activities.mastery_criterion: Matrix correctly identifies ferns as using spores, pines as using cones/naked seeds, and flowering plants as using fruits/seeds.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 30 mins observation of specimens, 30 mins matrix completion, 15 mins review.
activities.safety: Wash hands after handling plant materials.
activities.task: Students examine fern fronds with spores and pine cones, comparing them to a flowering plant, and fill out a classification matrix based on reproductive structures.

activities.differentiation: Provide sentence starters for the written definition.
activities.mastery_criterion: Written definition includes 'slow', 'directional', and 'growth response'.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 20 mins video and discussion, 30 mins writing, 25 mins peer review.
activities.task: Students watch a time-lapse video of a plant growing towards light, then write a definition of tropism and explain why time-lapse is needed to see it.

activities.differentiation: Include the prefix meanings (photo = light, hydro = water) at each station as a hint.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly identify gravitropism, phototropism, hydrotropism, and thigmotropism at the stations.
materials: Images or physical models of the four tropisms
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins instruction, 40 mins station rotation, 20 mins whole-class review.
activities.task: Students rotate through four stations showing images/models of different tropisms (roots down, stem to light, roots to water, vine on fence) and record the specific tropism name for each.

activities.differentiation: Use a physical model (like a folding book) to demonstrate the non-directional closing mechanism.
activities.mastery_criterion: Definition includes 'fast' and 'non-directional response'.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 25 mins video observation, 30 mins writing definition, 20 mins sharing.
activities.task: Students observe a video of a Venus flytrap and a Mimosa pudica closing, then write a definition of nastia focusing on speed and lack of directional growth.

activities.differentiation: Reduce the number of scenarios to sort for students who need more time to write justifications.
activities.mastery_criterion: Justifications correctly reference the speed (slow vs fast) and directionality (directional vs non-directional) of the movement.
materials: Sorting cards with plant movement scenarios
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins review of concepts, 40 mins sorting and justifying, 20 mins class debate on tricky cards.
activities.task: Students are given cards with descriptions of various plant movements and must sort them into 'Tropism' or 'Nastia', writing a justification for each based on speed and direction.

activities.differentiation: Allow students to work in pairs; one draws while the other writes the captions.
activities.mastery_criterion: Poster accurately depicts shoot/root systems and correctly describes transport/support functions.
materials: Reference books or printed materials on local plants
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins planning, 50 mins poster creation, 25 mins gallery walk.
activities.task: Students create a 'Plant Profile' poster for a chosen local plant, drawing its systems, labeling organs, and writing captions explaining how the stem and roots keep it alive.

activities.differentiation: Provide a pre-drawn chart for recording the height of the colored water over time.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students record accurate observations of water moving up the stem and reason that roots would have absorbed the water first.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 30 mins setup and initial observation, 60 mins follow-up observations (spread over days, consolidated here as active task time), 30 mins conclusion writing.
activities.safety: Use food-safe coloring. Do not consume the celery.
activities.task: Students place celery stalks in colored water and observe them over two days, recording the height of the color in the stem and predicting what would happen if the roots were still attached.

activities.differentiation: Provide a word bank for students who need vocabulary support.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly fill in 'roots', 'absorb', 'stem', and 'transport'.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instruction, 20 mins independent work, 15 mins self-correction.
activities.task: Students complete a quick 'fill-in-the-blank' paragraph about how water moves from the soil through the plant, relying only on memory.

activities.differentiation: Provide a visual diagram of a plant to point to while explaining.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students verbally include absorption by roots and transport by stems.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins modeling, 20 mins paired verbal explanations, 15 mins whole-class debrief.
activities.task: Students pair up and verbally explain to each other the journey of a water drop from the soil to the leaves, while the partner checks off key terms on a rubric.

activities.differentiation: Pre-cut the cardboard pieces for the maze to assist with fine motor skills.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students accurately record the directional growth of the stem toward the light and identify it as phototropism.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 45 mins maze construction and setup, 45 mins active observation recording (consolidated), 30 mins final analysis.
activities.safety: Ensure boxes are stable. Wash hands after handling soil.
activities.task: Students design a simple maze inside a cardboard box for a bean sprout to grow through towards a light hole, recording its phototropic response over a week.

activities.differentiation: Allow students to use abbreviations (e.g., 'Photo' for phototropism) if spelling is a barrier.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly identify the tropism in at least 3 out of 4 clips.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins setup, 20 mins video clips and responses, 15 mins discussion of clues.
activities.task: Students are shown four silent video clips of plant growth and must hold up a whiteboard with the correct tropism name for each.

activities.differentiation: Provide a comic template with the soil line already drawn.
activities.mastery_criterion: Comic strip accurately depicts roots growing down and stem growing up, with correct labels.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instruction, 25 mins drawing, 10 mins sharing.
activities.task: Students draw a comic strip showing a seed germinating underground, with roots showing gravitropism and the stem showing phototropism.

activities.differentiation: Provide bilingual labels if appropriate for the student population.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly identify the shoot/root systems and flowers/fruits of the provided local plants.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 20 mins introduction, 40 mins image analysis and labeling, 30 mins group discussion.
activities.task: Students analyze images of local agricultural plants, identifying their organ systems and reproductive parts, and discuss their importance.

activities.differentiation: Allow oral responses for students with severe writing difficulties.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly link symptoms to the failure of specific organs (e.g., wilting to root/stem failure or excessive transpiration).
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins instructions, 60 mins independent writing, 15 mins collection and wrap-up.
activities.task: Students complete a written performance task where they must diagnose a 'sick' plant based on symptoms (e.g., wilting, no fruits) and explain which organ system or process is failing.

activities.differentiation: Highlight key evidence words in the case studies for students who need reading support.
activities.mastery_criterion: Reports correctly classify reproduction methods and accurately differentiate between any tropisms or nasties described in the cases.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins instructions, 60 mins independent writing, 15 mins collection.
activities.task: Students evaluate a series of case studies of unusual plants (e.g., a fern growing on a wall, a Venus flytrap) and write a report classifying their reproduction and behavioral responses.

activities.differentiation: Allow sequencing and pointing to images before an oral explanation.
activities.mastery_criterion: Cites the differing growth directions and lighting conditions, then names a relevant contradictory observation such as both seedlings bending the same way despite different light directions.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes inspect and order records, 15 minutes compare evidence, 10 minutes propose a counter-observation, 10 minutes feedback.
activities.safety: Use images only; no prolonged plant manipulation or camera equipment is required.
activities.task: Compare two teacher-provided, time-stamped image sequences: one seedling bends toward a side light over several days, while another remains upright under overhead light. Identify the evidence supporting a directional growth response and propose one observation that would weaken that explanation. The images are supplied; no waiting time is counted.

activities.differentiation: Provide tactile models of symmetric shapes for students who benefit from physical manipulation.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly points to the central axis or lack thereof when asked.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes for introduction, 15 minutes for guided examples, 10 minutes for questions.
activities.safety: Ensure students remain seated during the presentation.
activities.task: Introduce bilateral, radial, and asymmetrical body plans using large printed photos of a butterfly, sea star, and sponge.

activities.differentiation: Provide cards with pre-drawn axes for students needing visual support.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly sorts at least 8 out of 10 animal cards.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes setup, 25 minutes sorting, 10 minutes review.
activities.safety: Ensure bins are placed on stable tables to prevent tipping.
activities.task: Sort cards of various animals into three bins labeled bilateral, radial, and asymmetrical.

activities.differentiation: Provide larger outlines for students with fine motor difficulties.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student accurately draws the correct number of symmetry lines for each animal outline.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instruction, 25 minutes drawing, 10 minutes peer review.
activities.safety: Instruct students on the safe use of rulers to avoid poking.
activities.task: Draw lines of symmetry on printed animal outlines using rulers.

activities.differentiation: Allow oral responses for students who struggle with writing.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly identifies the symmetry type of at least 4 out of 5 given animals.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes instructions, 25 minutes independent work.
activities.safety: Standard classroom safety during written assessment.
activities.task: Look at images of a butterfly, a sea star, and a sea sponge. State the type of symmetry for each.

activities.differentiation: Provide a personal copy of the diagram for close viewing.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student can verbally define metamorphosis and name the four stages in order when prompted.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 20 minutes explanation, 20 minutes interactive board work, 10 minutes summary.
activities.safety: Ensure clear pathways when students come to the board.
activities.task: Explain the mosquito life cycle using a step-by-step diagram on the board, explicitly defining 'metamorphosis' as the process encompassing these developmental stages.

activities.differentiation: Provide pre-cut stage images for students to paste instead of drawing.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly draws and labels the four stages in the correct order on the wheel.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes setup, 35 minutes crafting, 10 minutes sharing.
activities.safety: Supervise the use of brass fasteners to prevent skin pricks.
activities.task: Create a paper plate wheel showing the 4 stages of mosquito metamorphosis.

activities.differentiation: Highlight key words in the descriptions for reading support.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly matches all four descriptions and places them in chronological order.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes reading, 30 minutes matching and gluing, 15 minutes review.
activities.task: Match stage names to descriptions and sequence them on a timeline.

activities.differentiation: Provide larger cards for easier handling.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly orders the four stages of mosquito development.
materials: Sets of 4 stage cards per student
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes distribution, 25 minutes sequencing, 10 minutes collection.
activities.task: Arrange the cards showing egg, larva, pupa, and adult mosquito in the correct chronological order.

activities.differentiation: Use physical gestures (stepping forward/backward) to reinforce the concepts.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student can state whether moving toward a stimulus is positive or negative.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 20 minutes explanation, 15 minutes demonstration, 10 minutes Q&A.
activities.safety: Do not shine the flashlight directly into students' eyes.
activities.task: Define positive and negative taxism with examples like a moth to light and a worm away from light.

activities.differentiation: Provide scenarios with visual cues (arrows pointing toward or away).
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly classifies at least 5 out of 6 scenarios.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes reading, 30 minutes classifying, 15 minutes group discussion.
activities.task: Read 6 short scenarios of animal movements and classify them as positive or negative taxisms.

activities.differentiation: Allow students to use toy figures instead of their own bodies for the role-play.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student accurately demonstrates movement toward or away from the stimulus based on the card.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes instruction, 35 minutes role-play, 10 minutes debrief.
activities.safety: Ensure the role-play area is clear of obstacles to prevent tripping.
activities.task: Role-play taxisms based on prompt cards showing different stimuli.

activities.differentiation: Read the scenarios aloud for students with reading difficulties.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly classifies 3 out of 4 scenarios as positive or negative taxisms.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes instructions, 35 minutes independent work.
activities.task: Read 4 scenarios: a moth flying toward light, an earthworm moving away from light, a fish swimming toward food, and a cockroach hiding in the dark. Classify each movement.

activities.differentiation: Provide physical objects (tweezers, straws) to represent the structures during the explanation.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student can verbally link one structure to its specific feeding function.
materials: Large pictures of animal feeding structures
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 20 minutes presentation, 15 minutes interactive discussion, 10 minutes summary.
activities.safety: Ensure students remain seated during the presentation.
