activities.task: Students create a mechanical hand model by taping cut straws (bones) onto a paper hand outline and threading string (tendons/muscles) through them. Pulling the strings bends the paper fingers.

activities.differentiation: Allow oral explanations for students with writing difficulties.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student explicitly states that the muscle (string) pulls the bone (cardboard) to create movement at the joint.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes manipulating the model, 20 minutes writing the explanation.
activities.task: Using the previously built cardboard and string model of an arm, pull the string and write a short description of what happens to the cardboard pieces and how this relates to real muscles and bones.

activities.differentiation: Provide pre-drawn silhouettes for groups that need more time.
activities.mastery_criterion: Silhouette includes the brain in the head, spinal cord down the back, and nerves branching to limbs, color-coded correctly.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes explanation, 20 minutes drawing, 10 minutes review.
activities.task: Project a diagram of the nervous system. Explain the central (brain, spinal cord) and peripheral (nerves) parts. Have students trace a human silhouette on large paper and draw the brain, spinal cord, and nerves in different colors.

activities.differentiation: Pre-cut yarn lengths for students with fine motor challenges.
activities.mastery_criterion: Yarn is glued in the correct anatomical positions representing the three main components.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instruction, 25 minutes gluing yarn, 10 minutes drying and sharing.
activities.safety: Use blunt-tipped scissors. Avoid getting glue in eyes.
activities.task: Students use different colored yarn and glue to map the brain, spinal cord, and nerves onto a cardboard body outline.

activities.differentiation: Use high-contrast diagrams for visually impaired students.
activities.mastery_criterion: Diagram is accurately color-coded with a matching legend.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instruction, 25 minutes coloring, 10 minutes peer check.
activities.task: Students receive a detailed printed diagram of the human body and must color-code the brain red, the spinal cord blue, and the nerves yellow, then add a legend.

activities.differentiation: Provide a checklist of the three parts to ensure none are forgotten.
activities.mastery_criterion: Drawing shows the brain in the head, connected to a spinal cord running down the center, with nerves branching out to the arms and legs.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes instruction, 20 minutes drawing, 5 minutes collection.
activities.task: Draw the central and peripheral nervous system on a blank human silhouette, using different colors for the brain, spinal cord, and nerves.

activities.differentiation: Assign roles based on mobility and comfort levels.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students can verbally explain the sequence of the message passing from skin to brain.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 20 minutes explanation, 20 minutes role-play, 10 minutes debrief.
activities.safety: Ensure the ball is passed gently, not thrown.
activities.task: Explain the sensory pathway. Conduct a whole-class role-play where students act as the skin, nerves, spinal cord, and brain, passing a message (a ball) from the 'skin' to the 'brain' when a stimulus is introduced.

activities.differentiation: Provide pre-drawn panels that students only need to sequence and caption.
activities.mastery_criterion: Storyboard panels are in the correct chronological order showing the pathway to the brain.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instruction, 30 minutes drawing, 10 minutes sharing.
activities.task: Students draw a 4-panel storyboard illustrating the sequence of events when a person touches a cold ice cube, showing the stimulus, nerve transmission, spinal cord routing, and brain processing.

activities.differentiation: Use images on the cards alongside text for emerging readers.
activities.mastery_criterion: All card sets are ordered correctly from stimulus to brain.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instruction, 30 minutes sorting multiple sets, 10 minutes review.
activities.task: Students work in small groups to sort sets of cards representing different sensory scenarios (e.g., smelling a flower, hearing a bell) into the correct pathway order.

activities.differentiation: Read the cards aloud for students who need reading support.
activities.mastery_criterion: Sequence strictly follows: Skin touches hot surface -> Nerves detect heat -> Signal travels to spinal cord and brain -> Brain registers pain.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes instruction, 20 minutes sorting and gluing, 5 minutes collection.
activities.task: Order the provided cards to show what happens when you touch a hot surface, from the moment of touch to the brain registering pain.

activities.differentiation: Provide a graphic organizer for students to take notes during the discussion.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students contribute to a class chart detailing the step-by-step integration of the three systems.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 20 minutes demonstration and discussion, 25 minutes collaborative writing, 15 minutes review.
activities.safety: Ensure the dropped object is soft and lightweight.
activities.task: Present a scenario: catching a falling object. Discuss as a class how the eyes, brain, nerves, muscles, and bones work together. Model how to write a logical prediction of this coordinated response.

activities.differentiation: Provide sentence starters (e.g., 'First, the nerves in the foot...').
activities.mastery_criterion: Paragraph includes sensory input from the foot, brain processing, and muscle-bone interaction to lift the foot.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes scenario analysis, 30 minutes writing, 15 minutes peer review.
activities.safety: Standard classroom safety. Do not use real sharp stones.
activities.task: Students write a paragraph predicting the coordinated response of the nervous, muscular, and skeletal systems when a person steps on a sharp stone barefoot.

activities.differentiation: Provide a graphic organizer with three boxes (Sensory, Brain, Movement) to structure the response.
activities.mastery_criterion: Response includes sensory input (eyes), brain processing, and muscle-bone interaction for movement.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes reading scenario, 25 minutes writing.
activities.task: Read the scenario: You see a ball flying towards your face. Write a short paragraph predicting how your nervous, muscular, and skeletal systems will work together to catch or dodge it.

activities.differentiation: Allow bullet points instead of full sentences.
activities.mastery_criterion: Briefly mentions nerves detecting heat, brain processing, and muscles pulling arm bones away.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes prompt, 10 minutes writing, 5 minutes review.
activities.task: Quick write: Explain the system coordination that happens when you accidentally touch a hot plate and pull your hand away.

activities.differentiation: Provide a template with empty boxes and arrows.
activities.mastery_criterion: Flowchart shows ears -> nerves -> brain -> nerves -> neck muscles -> neck bones.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes prompt, 10 minutes drawing, 5 minutes holding up whiteboards for check.
activities.task: Draw a quick flowchart showing the system coordination when you hear a loud noise and turn your head to look.

activities.differentiation: Provide individual copies of the diagram for closer viewing.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students can point to the correct organs on the diagram when named.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 20 minutes instruction, 15 minutes guided identification, 10 minutes review.
activities.safety: Maintain a respectful and scientific environment. Do not ask students to relate this to their own bodies.
activities.task: Use an anatomical diagram to introduce the female reproductive system. Point out and explain the location of the ovaries, fallopian tubes, uterus, and vagina.

activities.differentiation: Provide a stencil for the basic shape.
activities.mastery_criterion: Playdough shapes roughly match the anatomical structure and are labeled correctly.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes setup, 25 minutes modeling and labeling, 10 minutes cleanup.
activities.safety: Wash hands after using playdough. Do not ingest.
activities.task: Students use playdough to create a 2D model of the female reproductive system on a paper plate, labeling the ovaries, fallopian tubes, uterus, and vagina with toothpick flags.

activities.differentiation: Include a brief description of the shape on the name card (e.g., 'almond-shaped' for ovaries).
activities.mastery_criterion: All organ names are correctly matched to their corresponding shapes.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instruction, 25 minutes playing the game, 10 minutes review.
activities.task: Students play a matching game where they match the name of the female reproductive organ to a card showing its specific shape isolated from the rest of the system.

activities.differentiation: Provide a word bank.
activities.mastery_criterion: At least 3 out of 4 organs are correctly labeled.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes instruction, 20 minutes labeling, 5 minutes collection.
activities.task: Given a diagram of the female reproductive system, label the ovaries, fallopian tubes, uterus, and vagina.

activities.differentiation: Provide individual copies of the diagram for closer viewing.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students can point to the correct organs on the diagram when named.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 20 minutes instruction, 15 minutes guided identification, 10 minutes review.
activities.safety: Maintain a respectful and scientific environment. Do not ask students to relate this to their own bodies.
activities.task: Use an anatomical diagram to introduce the male reproductive system. Point out and explain the location of the testes, vas deferens, urethra, and penis.

activities.differentiation: Provide a stencil for the basic shape.
activities.mastery_criterion: Playdough shapes roughly match the anatomical structure and are labeled correctly.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes setup, 25 minutes modeling and labeling, 10 minutes cleanup.
activities.safety: Wash hands after using playdough. Do not ingest.
activities.task: Students use playdough to create a 2D model of the male reproductive system on a paper plate, labeling the testes, vas deferens, urethra, and penis with toothpick flags.

activities.differentiation: Include a brief description of the shape on the name card.
activities.mastery_criterion: All organ names are correctly matched to their corresponding shapes.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instruction, 25 minutes playing the game, 10 minutes review.
activities.task: Students play a matching game where they match the name of the male reproductive organ to a card showing its specific shape isolated from the rest of the system.

activities.differentiation: Provide a word bank.
activities.mastery_criterion: At least 3 out of 4 organs are correctly labeled.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes instruction, 20 minutes labeling, 5 minutes collection.
activities.task: Given a diagram of the male reproductive system, label the testes, vas deferens, urethra, and penis.

activities.differentiation: Use picture cards of the organs to place on the board alongside the words.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly identify which system each organ belongs to during the class discussion.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes review of organs, 20 minutes sorting activity, 5 minutes summary.
activities.task: Create a large two-column chart on the board (Male / Female). Discuss each organ learned previously and have the class decide which column it belongs in, writing them down.

activities.differentiation: Include diagrams on the cards for visual support.
activities.mastery_criterion: All cards are placed in the correct box.
materials: Small boxes labeled Male and Female
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instruction, 20 minutes sorting, 10 minutes checking answers.
activities.task: Students work in pairs with a deck of cards containing names of reproductive organs. They must sort them into two physical boxes labeled 'Male' and 'Female'.

activities.differentiation: Provide pre-drawn columns and organ stickers.
activities.mastery_criterion: Poster accurately separates male and female organs into distinct columns.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes planning, 25 minutes creating poster, 5 minutes cleanup.
activities.task: Students create a comparative poster with two columns, drawing one key organ for each system and listing the other organs below it.

activities.differentiation: Read the list of organs aloud.
activities.mastery_criterion: All 6 organs are placed in the correct column.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes instruction, 20 minutes sorting, 5 minutes collection.
activities.task: Sort the following organs into a two-column table for Male and Female: Uterus, Testes, Ovaries, Prostate, Vagina, Vas Deferens.

activities.differentiation: Use fewer organs for students who need a modified workload.
activities.mastery_criterion: Lines correctly connect organs to the appropriate biological sex.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes instruction, 10 minutes completing worksheet, 5 minutes review.
activities.task: Students complete a quick worksheet where they draw a line connecting the organ name to either a 'Male' or 'Female' icon.

activities.differentiation: Allow students to confer with a partner before raising their card.
activities.mastery_criterion: Majority of the class holds up the correct color card for each organ.
materials: Blue and yellow cards for each student
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes distribution, 15 minutes flashcard activity.
activities.task: Teacher holds up a flashcard with an organ name. Students hold up a blue card for male or a yellow card for female.

activities.differentiation: Provide a guided notes sheet.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students can verbally link the hormones to the correct biological sex and state their general purpose.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 25 minutes instruction, 20 minutes Q&A and checking for understanding.
activities.safety: Keep discussions strictly biological and general. Avoid discussing personal timelines for puberty to prevent stigmatization.
activities.task: Direct instruction explaining that puberty involves bodily changes caused by sex hormones. Introduce Testosterone (primarily male) and Estrogen/Progesterone (primarily female). Discuss their role in initiating physical changes.

activities.differentiation: Use color-coding to help guide the matches.
activities.mastery_criterion: Matches are made correctly, showing the relationship between hormones, sex, and puberty.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes instruction, 25 minutes matching, 10 minutes review.
activities.task: Students complete a matching activity linking 'Testosterone' and 'Estrogen/Progesterone' to 'Male' and 'Female', and linking both to 'Causes physical changes during puberty'.

activities.differentiation: Provide a template with headings already printed.
activities.mastery_criterion: Brochure accurately names the hormones and their role in puberty.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes planning, 30 minutes creating brochure, 5 minutes cleanup.
activities.safety: Ensure content remains abstract and scientific.
activities.task: Students create a simple, abstract informational brochure explaining what hormones are and how they trigger the changes of puberty in males and females.

activities.differentiation: Provide sentence starters for the written portion.
activities.mastery_criterion: Testosterone matches Male. Estrogen/Progesterone match Female. Sentence states they cause bodily changes during puberty.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes instruction, 20 minutes independent work, 5 minutes collection.
activities.task: Match the hormone to the biological sex it primarily affects during puberty, and write one sentence explaining why these hormones are important.

activities.differentiation: Provide a printed chart with examples of each joint type.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students can verbally classify a given joint as immobile, semi-mobile, or mobile.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes introduction, 20 minutes physical demonstration and practice, 10 minutes review.
activities.safety: Ensure students move gently to avoid injury.
activities.task: Introduce the three types of joints (immobile, semi-mobile, mobile) using a presentation and physical demonstrations. Have students move their own bodies to feel the difference between mobile joints (knees, elbows) and semi-mobile joints (spine), and point to immobile joints (skull).

activities.differentiation: Use tactile or high-contrast flashcards for students with visual impairments.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students can correctly pair each sense with its corresponding organ.
materials: Large chart of the five senses
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 20 minutes instruction, 15 minutes guided practice with flashcards, 10 minutes review.
activities.task: Introduce the five senses (sight, hearing, smell, taste, touch) and their corresponding organs (eyes, ears, nose, tongue, skin) using a large chart. Discuss how each organ helps us perceive the environment.

activities.differentiation: Provide color-coded diagrams for easier identification.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students can point to the correct areas on a diagram when the lobes and cerebellum are named.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 20 minutes instruction, 15 minutes guided identification, 10 minutes review.
activities.task: Project a diagram of the brain and introduce the frontal, parietal, occipital, and temporal lobes, as well as the cerebellum. Explain their locations and have students point to the approximate areas on their own heads.

activities.differentiation: Provide a glossary of terms.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students can verbally define fertilization and menstruation and state where they occur.
materials: Diagrams of the female reproductive system
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 25 minutes instruction, 20 minutes Q&A and review.
activities.safety: Maintain a respectful and scientific environment.
activities.task: Explain the basic processes of fertilization (meeting of ovocyte and male gamete in the oviducts) and menstruation (shedding of the endometrium from the uterus if no fertilization occurs) using simple, age-appropriate diagrams.

activities.differentiation: Provide a checklist of care practices.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students can list at least three appropriate care practices.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes discussion, 15 minutes brainstorming, 10 minutes review.
activities.safety: Maintain a respectful and scientific environment.
activities.task: Discuss the importance of hygiene and care for the reproductive system. Brainstorm a list of care practices (e.g., daily bathing, clean underwear) and write them on the board.

activities.differentiation: Provide a visual sorting mat with icons representing fundamental vs derived concepts for students who need visual aids.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly classify at least 8 out of 10 provided units into the correct columns.
materials: Everyday product packaging with measurement labels
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins introduction and label observation, 30 mins chart creation and classification, 15 mins class review and correction.
activities.safety: Ensure product packaging is clean and free of allergens or hazardous residues.
activities.task: Students review a set of everyday objects and their labels (e.g., a 1 L bottle, a 500 g bag of beans). They create a two-column chart in their notebooks, classifying the units found on the labels into fundamental SI units and derived SI units based on a reference table provided by the teacher.

activities.differentiation: Provide a checklist of the 4 main SI rules (lowercase, no plural, space, no period) for quick reference.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students identify and correct at least 4 out of 5 formatting errors using proper SI rules.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins rule explanation, 30 mins editing task, 20 mins peer review and discussion.
activities.task: Students receive a 'badly written' science report containing multiple SI formatting errors (e.g., 5Kgs, 10 M, 20secs). They must act as editors, crossing out the errors and writing the correct SI format above them, then write a short rule justification for each correction.

activities.differentiation: Use digital balances or stopwatches with large displays for students with visual impairments.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students record measurements with the correct numerical value and unit, within the tolerance of the instruments used.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins station instructions, 60 mins rotating through stations (20 mins each), 15 mins data comparison.
activities.safety: Ensure pendulums are swung in clear areas to avoid hitting anyone. Heavy rocks should be handled carefully to avoid dropping on toes.
activities.task: Students rotate through three measurement stations: Length (measuring a desk with a meter stick), Mass (measuring a rock with a balance), and Time (timing a pendulum swing with a stopwatch). They record their direct measurements in a structured data table.

activities.differentiation: Provide formula cards with step-by-step calculation templates (fill-in-the-blank style) for students who struggle with multi-step math.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly apply the volume and density formulas, arriving at accurate derived quantities with proper units.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 20 mins direct measurement, 40 mins calculations, 30 mins sharing and verifying results.
activities.task: Students measure the three dimensions of a rectangular block to calculate its volume. Then, they measure its mass and use the calculated volume to determine its density. They record all steps and final derived quantities in their notebooks.

activities.differentiation: Allow the use of calculators and provide a worked example at the top of the worksheet.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students successfully convert at least 3 out of 4 measurements, showing correct mathematical steps.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 20 mins explanation of conversion factors, 50 mins conversion practice, 20 mins review.
activities.task: Students are given a recipe or a building plan with measurements in non-SI units (e.g., inches, pounds). They use provided conversion factors to translate all measurements into SI units, showing their multiplication or division steps clearly.

activities.differentiation: Use number lines to visually show which rounded number the raw decimal is closer to.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly round 4 out of 5 numbers to the specified decimal places.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins rule review, 30 mins rounding practice, 15 mins peer checking.
activities.task: Students receive a set of raw calculator outputs from division problems (e.g., 10/3 = 3.333333). They practice applying the three rounding rules to round these numbers to one and two decimal places, explaining which rule they used for each.

activities.differentiation: Color-code the exponent sign (positive for large, negative for small) on introductory cards.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly match all cards and write at least two valid original examples of scientific notation.
materials: Sets of matching cards (standard vs scientific notation)
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins explanation, 30 mins matching game, 15 mins independent writing.
activities.task: Students play a matching game where they pair cards showing standard large/small numbers (e.g., distance to the sun, size of a cell) with their corresponding scientific notation cards. They then write three of their own examples.

activities.differentiation: Provide sentence starters for the justification (e.g., 'The throws were precise because...').
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly identify the precision and accuracy of the target hits and provide a logical justification based on the definitions.
materials: Target drawn on the board or poster
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 20 mins throwing activity, 20 mins group analysis, 20 mins writing justifications.
activities.safety: Ensure paper balls are only thrown at the designated target. Clean up any water spills immediately to prevent slipping.
activities.task: Students throw wet paper balls at a drawn target on the board. They analyze the grouping of the hits to determine if the throws were precise (grouped together), accurate (near the center), both, or neither, and write a short justification.

activities.differentiation: Read the case studies aloud for students with reading difficulties and discuss the errors orally before writing.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly categorize the error in 3 out of 4 case studies and provide a plausible prevention method.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins introduction to error types, 30 mins case study analysis, 15 mins class discussion.
activities.task: Students read a series of short case studies describing failed scientific experiments or measurements. They must highlight the source of the error, categorize it as personal, instrumental, or environmental, and propose a way to prevent it.

activities.differentiation: Provide a step-by-step calculation template that breaks the error propagation formula into smaller, manageable math operations.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly calculate the area and apply the error propagation formula to find the final uncertainty.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 20 mins measuring and identifying instrument error, 40 mins area and error calculations, 30 mins reviewing steps.
activities.task: Students measure the dimensions of their textbook using a ruler, noting the instrument's minimum division as the error. They calculate the area of the book cover and apply the taught formula to find the propagated error of the area.

activities.differentiation: Allow students to use their reference charts from previous lessons.
activities.mastery_criterion: All 10 quantities are correctly classified and formatted according to SI rules.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instructions, 40 mins creating passports, 10 mins sharing.
activities.task: Students create a 'Measurement Passport' where they list 5 fundamental and 5 derived quantities, writing their correct SI symbols and formatting a hypothetical measurement for each.

activities.differentiation: Pair students so one can focus on timing while the other focuses on releasing the car.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students accurately record distance and time, and correctly calculate speed using the v=d/t formula.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 20 mins setup, 40 mins data collection, 30 mins calculations.
activities.safety: Ensure cars are rolled in designated areas so no one trips on them.
activities.task: Students build a small ramp and roll a toy car down it. They measure the distance of the ramp and the time it takes the car to reach the bottom, then calculate the derived quantity of speed.

activities.differentiation: Provide the conversion factors directly next to each problem in the maze.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students successfully navigate the maze by correctly solving at least 80% of the conversion problems.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instructions, 40 mins maze solving, 10 mins checking the path.
activities.task: Students solve a 'conversion maze' worksheet where the correct converted answer leads them to the next problem, eventually guiding them to the finish line.

activities.differentiation: Provide a visual guide showing how to count decimal places for the exponent.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly round and convert at least 4 out of 5 complex numbers.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins review, 35 mins independent practice, 10 mins review.
activities.task: Students are given a list of highly precise astronomical and microscopic data (e.g., 0.000004567 m). They must first round the numbers to three significant figures, then convert the rounded numbers into scientific notation.

activities.differentiation: Provide a paragraph template with fill-in-the-blanks for key terms.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students write a coherent paragraph correctly identifying the accuracy/precision state and logically categorizing the error source.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins reading the report, 30 mins writing the analysis, 15 mins sharing.
activities.task: Students analyze a mock lab report that contains flawed data. They must write a short paragraph evaluating the precision and accuracy of the data and identifying whether the likely cause was a personal, instrumental, or environmental error.

activities.differentiation: Provide the specific cubic conversion factor (1 m3 = 1,000,000 cm3) explicitly.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly calculate the initial volume and successfully apply the cubic conversion factor.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 30 mins measuring and initial calculation, 40 mins conversion, 20 mins review.
activities.task: Students calculate the volume of a large box in cubic centimeters, then use conversion factors to convert their final derived answer into cubic meters.

activities.differentiation: Allow students to work in pairs to verify each other's math steps.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly apply the error propagation formula to the classroom area calculation.
materials: Worksheets with provided measurements and errors
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins setup, 40 mins calculations, 10 mins review.
activities.task: Students practice error propagation by calculating the area of the classroom floor using measurements provided by the teacher, including the instrumental error of the measuring tape used.

activities.differentiation: Provide a visual diagram of the water displacement method.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students successfully determine the density and logically identify at least one source of error in their method.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 30 mins experimental design, 40 mins execution and measurement, 30 mins calculations, 20 mins error analysis.
activities.safety: Wipe up any spilled water immediately to prevent slipping. Handle glass cylinders with care.
activities.task: Students design an experiment to find the density of an irregularly shaped object (like a stone) using water displacement. They must record direct measurements, calculate the derived density, and identify any potential errors in their procedure.

activities.differentiation: Provide a structured comparison table to help organize the data from both instruments.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students justify their choice of instrument based on calculated error propagation and concepts of precision/accuracy.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 40 mins data collection with both instruments, 50 mins calculations, 30 mins writing conclusions.
activities.task: Students compare two different measuring instruments (e.g., a standard ruler vs a tailor's tape) by measuring the same object multiple times. They analyze the precision and accuracy of both, calculate the area and propagated error using data from both, and conclude which instrument is better for the task.

activities.differentiation: Allow extra time and provide a quiet environment for students who need it.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students score at least 80% on the combined tasks according to the specific scoring rules of each micro-skill.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instructions, 50 mins assessment completion.
activities.task: Students complete a comprehensive written and practical test where they classify units, correct formatting, take a direct measurement of a provided object, calculate its volume, and convert the result to a different unit.

activities.differentiation: Allow extra time and provide a quiet environment for students who need it.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students score at least 80% on the combined tasks according to the specific scoring rules of each micro-skill.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instructions, 50 mins assessment completion.
activities.task: Students complete a written test involving rounding data, converting to scientific notation, analyzing a data set for precision/accuracy, classifying described errors, and performing one error propagation calculation.

activities.differentiation: Allow the use of calculators.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly calculate the density for all three materials.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 mins setup, 15 mins calculation race, 10 mins review.
activities.task: Students are given a quick 'flash' challenge on the board with mass and volume data for three mystery materials. They race to calculate the density of each.

activities.differentiation: Provide the formulas at the top of the page.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students accurately fill in the missing derived values using the correct formulas.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 mins instructions, 20 mins calculations, 5 mins review.
activities.task: Students review a previous lab's data table that has missing derived values (speed and volume). They must recalculate the missing values from the provided direct measurements.

activities.differentiation: Pair students up to play on a single card.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly identify and mark the rounded numbers, achieving a 'Bingo'.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 mins rules, 20 mins gameplay, 5 mins verification.
activities.task: Students play a quick game of 'Rounding Bingo' where the teacher calls out raw decimals and a rounding rule (e.g., 'round to one decimal place'), and students mark the correct rounded number on their cards.

activities.differentiation: Allow the use of calculators for the final addition.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly round all prices and find the accurate total.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 mins instructions, 20 mins rounding and adding, 5 mins review.
activities.task: Students are given a grocery receipt with prices having three decimal places (hypothetical scenario). They must round all prices to two decimal places (standard currency format) and calculate the new total.

activities.differentiation: Walk through the first calculation together as a class on the board.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students successfully integrate the error propagation formula with their prior density calculations.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins concept bridge explanation, 30 mins calculations, 15 mins review.
activities.task: Students revisit their density calculations from a previous lesson. The teacher introduces the concept that the mass and volume measurements had errors. Students now apply the error propagation formula to their previously calculated derived density.

activities.differentiation: Provide a scaled drawing of the path on paper for students with mobility issues to measure with a ruler instead.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly record a larger value for distance than displacement and define distance as the path taken and displacement as the straight-line change in position.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins setup and instruction, 30 mins physical activity and measurement, 15 mins recording and discussion.
activities.safety: Ensure the walking path is clear of tripping hazards.
activities.task: Students walk a specific path marked on the classroom floor (e.g., 3 steps forward, 4 steps right). They measure the total path length with a measuring tape (distance) and then measure the straight line from start to finish (displacement). They record both values and write a definition for each based on their physical experience.

activities.differentiation: Use maps with larger, color-coded grid lines (e.g., red for latitude, blue for longitude) for visual support.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students accurately place dots at the correct intersections of latitude and longitude for all 3 given coordinates.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 20 mins modeling and explanation, 30 mins guided practice, 10 mins review.
activities.task: Students receive a map with a latitude and longitude grid. The teacher models finding a specific coordinate. Students then practice finding 3 specific coordinates provided by the teacher, marking them with a dot, and writing the name of the feature located there.

activities.differentiation: Provide pre-filled time intervals on the data sheet so students only need to focus on recording position.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly calculate equal distances for equal time intervals and explicitly state both MRU conditions (straight line, constant speed).
materials: Video or simulation of constant speed motion
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins introduction, 30 mins data collection and calculation, 15 mins conclusion writing.
activities.task: Students analyze a video or simulation of a car moving along a straight track. They record the car's position every 2 seconds in a data table. They calculate the distance covered in each interval, observe that it is constant, and write a statement classifying the motion as MRU based on the straight path and constant speed.

activities.differentiation: Provide a visual checklist of MCU characteristics for students to check off as they observe.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly calculate the period of rotation and justify the MCU classification using the circular trajectory and constant rotation rate.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins setup, 30 mins observation and timing, 15 mins writing classification.
activities.safety: Ensure spinning objects are stable and students keep fingers away from moving spokes.
activities.task: Students observe a marked spinning object (like a bicycle wheel or a top). They use a stopwatch to time how long it takes for the mark to complete 5 full rotations, then calculate the time per rotation. They write a paragraph classifying the motion as MCU, citing the circular path and constant time per rotation.

activities.differentiation: Provide pre-drawn force arrows that students must label and balance, reducing the drawing burden.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly draw canceling force arrows and predict either rest or constant velocity, citing zero net force.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 20 mins direct instruction on Newton's First Law, 30 mins scenario analysis, 10 mins sharing predictions.
activities.task: Students analyze scenarios presented on cards (e.g., a book resting on a table, a hockey puck gliding on frictionless ice). For each, they draw force arrows (gravity, normal force, applied force, friction). If forces cancel out (net force zero), they predict the resulting motion (rest or constant velocity) and justify their reasoning in writing.

activities.differentiation: Provide a fill-in-the-blank template for the justification paragraph.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly identify the handle position as requiring the least force and justify this by referencing the longer lever arm distance from the axis of rotation.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 20 mins physical experience with doors, 20 mins diagramming, 20 mins writing justifications.
activities.safety: Ensure fingers are not pinched in the door hinges.
activities.task: Students push a classroom door closed using one finger at three different points: near the hinge, in the middle, and near the handle. They rank the points by how much effort was required. They then draw a diagram of the door, labeling the axis of rotation and the lever arm distances, and write a justification for why the handle position is most effective.

activities.differentiation: Use highly visual, color-coded springs where compression is obvious.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly identify only the stretched/compressed objects as having elastic potential energy and illustrate the deformation.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins introduction, 30 mins hands-on categorization and drawing, 15 mins review.
activities.safety: Require safety goggles when manipulating stretched rubber bands or springs to prevent eye injury.
activities.task: Students examine various objects: a relaxed rubber band, a stretched rubber band, an uncompressed spring, and a compressed spring. They categorize which objects currently store elastic potential energy and draw diagrams showing the deformation that causes the stored energy.

activities.differentiation: Provide a structured data table with pre-labeled height columns.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students record deeper craters for greater heights and conclude that higher elevation means greater gravitational potential energy.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins setup, 30 mins dropping and measuring, 15 mins writing conclusions.
activities.safety: Ensure sand is not thrown; sweep up any spills immediately to prevent slipping.
activities.task: Students drop a small ball into a container of sand from three different heights (0.5m, 1m, 1.5m). They measure the depth of the crater formed each time as an indicator of energy. They record the data and write a conclusion comparing the gravitational potential energy at the different heights.

activities.differentiation: Use a digital speedometer app (if teacher-operated) to make the speed difference concrete.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students measure a greater push distance for the faster car and conclude that higher speed results in greater kinetic energy.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins setup, 30 mins rolling and measuring, 15 mins writing comparisons.
activities.safety: Keep rolling objects on the floor or tables; do not launch them in the air.
activities.task: Students roll a toy car down a ramp into a lightweight block. They do this from a low release point (slow speed at bottom) and a high release point (fast speed at bottom). They measure how far the block is pushed each time. They write a statement comparing the kinetic energy of the car at the two different speeds.

activities.differentiation: Provide a diagram template of the pendulum swing for students to label.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly label max potential at the top, max kinetic at the bottom, and justify the continuous transformation between height and speed.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins building, 20 mins observation and diagramming, 25 mins writing justification.
activities.safety: Ensure weights are securely tied so they do not fly off during swinging.
activities.task: Students build a simple pendulum with string and a washer. They release it and observe the swing. They draw the pendulum at three positions: highest point, lowest point, and opposite highest point. They label where potential energy is max/min and where kinetic energy is max/min, and write a paragraph justifying how energy transforms between the two forms during the swing.

activities.differentiation: Allow students to use smaller tabletop grids and toy figures if outdoor mobility is an issue.
activities.mastery_criterion: Accurate measurement of both path distance and straight-line displacement, clearly distinguishing the two in their presentation.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 30 mins designing and drawing grid, 30 mins measuring, 30 mins presentations.
activities.safety: Ensure the playground surface is safe and obstacles are not tripping hazards.
activities.task: Students design an obstacle course on a grid drawn on the playground. They map a path through the obstacles, measure the total distance of the path, and then measure the direct displacement from start to finish. They present their map and measurements to the class.

activities.differentiation: Provide a magnifying glass for students who have difficulty reading small map print.
activities.mastery_criterion: Correct identification of at least 4 out of 5 locations based on the coordinates.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instructions, 40 mins independent practice, 10 mins peer review.
activities.task: Students receive a list of 5 geographic coordinates. They must locate each on a provided map, identify the geographical feature or city at that location, and record it in a table.

activities.differentiation: Provide pre-drawn axes on the graph paper.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students produce a linear graph and correctly argue that the constant slope indicates constant speed, fulfilling MRU criteria.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 30 mins setup and data collection, 30 mins graphing, 30 mins analysis and writing.
activities.safety: Clean up any oil spills immediately to prevent slipping. Do not ingest the oil.
activities.task: Students set up a tall clear bottle filled with oil. They drop a small bead into the oil and use a stopwatch to time its descent past evenly spaced marks on the bottle. They graph position vs. time and use the straight-line graph to justify classifying the motion as MRU.

activities.differentiation: Have students work in pairs: one spins and one times/counts.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly apply the definition of MCU to evaluate their own experimental setup, noting variations in rotation speed.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 20 mins setup, 40 mins experimentation and data collection, 30 mins report writing.
activities.safety: Ensure the salad spinner lid is securely fastened before spinning.
activities.task: Students build a simple centrifuge using a salad spinner. They place a small marked object inside, spin it at a steady rate, and attempt to count rotations per 10 seconds. They analyze the difficulty of maintaining constant angular speed and write a report on whether their manual spinning truly achieved MCU.

activities.differentiation: Use only horizontal or vertical forces (no angles) to simplify net force calculation.
activities.mastery_criterion: Accurate calculation of net force and correct prediction of motion state based on Newton's First Law.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins review of vector addition, 35 mins independent practice, 10 mins review.
activities.task: Students are given a worksheet with 5 diagrams of objects with various force vectors applied. They must calculate the net force for each. If the net force is zero, they predict the object's motion state (rest or constant velocity) and justify it.

activities.differentiation: Provide a structured data table and graph axes.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students collect accurate force data showing less force is needed further from the hinge, and justify this using the concept of lever arm and torque.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 30 mins data collection, 30 mins graphing, 30 mins analysis and conclusion.
activities.safety: Ensure students do not pull the spring scales beyond their maximum limit to prevent snapping.
activities.task: Students use a spring scale to pull open a heavy door from three different measured distances from the hinge. They record the force required at each distance. They graph Force vs. Distance from Hinge and write a conclusion justifying the inverse relationship based on torque requirements.

activities.differentiation: Pre-cut the cardboard tubes for students who struggle with scissors.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly identify that greater stretch (deformation) stores more elastic potential energy, evidenced by the longer launch distance.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 40 mins building launchers, 30 mins testing and measuring, 20 mins writing summary.
activities.safety: Students must wear safety goggles. Never aim launchers at people.
activities.task: Students build a simple rubber band launcher using cardboard tubes. They measure how far a paper ball is launched when the rubber band is pulled back 2 cm, 4 cm, and 6 cm. They record the data and write a summary identifying how the stretch distance relates to the stored elastic potential energy.

activities.differentiation: Provide a step-by-step experimental procedure checklist.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly isolate variables, showing that greater height (more potential energy) and greater mass (more kinetic energy) both result in the cup sliding further.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 20 mins setup, 40 mins conducting trials, 30 mins report writing.
activities.safety: Keep marbles on the floor to prevent slipping hazards.
activities.task: Students roll marbles of different masses down a ramp from different heights into a plastic cup. They measure how far the cup slides. They conduct trials varying only height (to test gravitational potential) and then varying only mass (to test kinetic energy impact). They write a report comparing the effects.

activities.differentiation: Provide a word bank (e.g., increases, decreases, transforms, maximum, minimum).
activities.mastery_criterion: Accurate justification of energy states at all 4 points, clearly describing the continuous transformation between potential and kinetic energy.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 20 mins review of concepts, 50 mins independent analysis and writing, 20 mins peer review.
activities.task: Students analyze a diagram of a roller coaster track with 4 labeled points. They must write a paragraph for each point, justifying the relative amounts of potential and kinetic energy based on the height and expected speed, and explaining the transformations between points.

activities.differentiation: Allow extra time or oral explanation of reasoning for students with writing difficulties.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students score 80% or higher on the rubric, demonstrating accurate application and reasoning across all kinematics and dynamics micros.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instructions, 50 mins assessment completion.
activities.task: Students complete a written assessment featuring scenario-based questions requiring them to calculate displacement, read map coordinates, classify motion types from data tables, predict motion from force diagrams, and justify torque applications.

activities.differentiation: Provide larger diagrams and clear, bold text.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students score 80% or higher on the rubric, demonstrating accurate identification, comparison, and reasoning regarding mechanical energy.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins instructions, 50 mins assessment completion.
activities.task: Students complete a written assessment analyzing diagrams of mechanical systems (springs, ramps, pendulums), comparing energy states, and justifying energy transformations.

activities.differentiation: Read the movements slowly and write them on the board as well.
activities.mastery_criterion: Accurate drawing of the path and correct calculation of both distance and displacement.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 mins instructions, 15 mins drawing and calculating, 10 mins partner comparison.
activities.task: Students are given a blank grid and a starting point. The teacher reads a sequence of movements. Students draw the path, calculate total distance, and draw/measure the displacement vector. They compare answers with a partner.

activities.differentiation: Highlight the start and end points in different colors.
activities.mastery_criterion: Correct identification of the longest distance and displacement, with a clear explanation distinguishing path length from straight-line change.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 mins instructions, 20 mins independent work, 5 mins review.
activities.task: Students analyze three pre-drawn paths on a grid. They must identify which path has the longest distance, which has the longest displacement, and write a sentence explaining why the two answers are different.

activities.differentiation: Pause the video at key points to allow students time to sketch.
activities.mastery_criterion: Accurate justification of energy transformation, noting max potential at the edges and max kinetic at the bottom.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins video observation, 20 mins sketching and writing.
activities.task: Students watch a short video of a skateboarder in a half-pipe. They sketch the half-pipe, mark three positions, and write a brief justification of how potential and kinetic energy transform as the skater moves back and forth.

activities.differentiation: Provide a template with sentence starters for the explanations.
activities.mastery_criterion: Correct sequencing of cards and accurate description of energy transformations at each stage.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 mins instructions, 20 mins sequencing and writing, 5 mins review.
activities.task: Students are given a set of cards showing different stages of a bouncing ball. They must sequence the cards and write a sentence for each transition explaining the energy transformation occurring (e.g., falling: potential to kinetic; hitting ground: kinetic to elastic potential).

activities.differentiation: Provide the first two points pre-plotted.
activities.mastery_criterion: Accurate plotting of points and correct calculation showing displacement is zero for a closed loop.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins math review, 30 mins plotting and calculating, 15 mins discussion on zero displacement.
activities.task: Students review Cartesian coordinate graphing from math class. They plot a series of points to form a shape, then calculate the distance of the perimeter and the displacement from the first point to the last point (which should be zero if closed).

activities.differentiation: Provide pre-marked paths for students who need scaffolding with measurement.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students accurately measure and sum the path segments for distance and correctly measure the straight-line displacement, explaining the difference.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 20 mins planning, 40 mins measuring outdoors, 30 mins data comparison and discussion.
activities.safety: Ensure the courtyard is clear of obstacles and students walk safely.
activities.task: Students work in groups to map out a multi-leg journey across the school courtyard. They use measuring tapes to record the distance of each leg and sum them up for the total distance. Finally, they measure the straight-line displacement from the start to the end point and compare the two values.

context_tasks.seismic-risk: Students use a detailed map of El Salvador to locate specific volcanoes and national parks given their latitude and longitude coordinates. They record the name of the feature found at each coordinate.

activities.differentiation: Use maps with larger print and highlighted grid lines for visual support.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly identify at least 4 out of 5 geographical features based on the provided coordinates.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins review, 50 mins map work, 25 mins sharing findings.
activities.task: Students use a detailed map of the supplied location to locate specific volcanoes and national parks given their latitude and longitude coordinates. They record the name of the feature found at each coordinate.

activities.differentiation: Provide a structured chart for categorizing the materials.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly identify that all deformed elastic objects store energy and rank them qualitatively based on stiffness and stretch.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 20 mins setup, 40 mins testing, 30 mins categorization and writing.
activities.safety: Students must wear safety goggles when stretching rubber bands.
activities.task: Students test different elastic materials (various rubber bands, soft springs) by stretching them to different lengths and observing the force required. They categorize the materials based on how much elastic potential energy they seem to store when deformed.

activities.differentiation: Pause videos to allow extra processing time.
activities.mastery_criterion: Correct classification of MRU and MCU with accurate reference to trajectory and constant speed/rotation.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 mins video viewing, 15 mins writing, 5 mins review.
activities.task: Students are shown 4 short video clips of different motions (a car on a straight highway, a spinning fan, a bouncing ball, a pendulum). They must quickly classify each as MRU, MCU, or neither, and write one sentence justifying their choice.

activities.differentiation: Provide diagrams with only horizontal forces for simplicity.
activities.mastery_criterion: Accurate net force calculation and correct prediction of the motion state.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 mins instructions, 20 mins quiz, 5 mins self-correction.
activities.task: Students receive a quick quiz with 3 force diagrams. They must calculate the net force for each and predict if the object will remain at rest/constant velocity or accelerate.

context_tasks.protected-areas: Students connect their social studies knowledge of El Salvador's departments with geographic coordinates. They are given a list of departments and must find their approximate center coordinates on a map.

activities.differentiation: Provide a list of coordinate options to match with the departments.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students accurately determine the latitude and longitude for at least 3 departments.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 mins social studies review, 30 mins map work, 15 mins discussion.
activities.task: Students connect their social studies knowledge of the supplied location's departments with geographic coordinates. They are given a list of departments and must find their approximate center coordinates on a map.

activities.differentiation: Provide a pre-drawn outline for students who struggle with fine motor skills.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly label the nucleus, protons, neutrons, and electrons in their notebook diagrams.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes for introduction and drawing on the board, 20 minutes for students to copy and label, 10 minutes for review and correction.
activities.safety: Standard classroom safety. Ensure students do not share colored pencils if health protocols require it.
activities.task: Introduce the atomic model by drawing a large diagram on the board. Explain the nucleus, protons, neutrons, and electrons. Students copy the diagram into their notebooks and label each part using colored pencils.

activities.differentiation: Allow students to work in pairs if they need help manipulating the playdough.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students construct a model with a central nucleus containing protons and neutrons, and electrons on the outside, correctly labeled.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes for setup and instructions, 25 minutes for building and labeling, 10 minutes for a gallery walk to see peers' models.
activities.safety: Ensure students do not ingest the playdough. Wash hands after the activity.
activities.task: Students use playdough of three different colors to build a 3D model of an atom. They use toothpicks and paper flags to label the nucleus, protons, neutrons, and electrons.

activities.differentiation: Highlight the nucleus in a specific color for visually impaired students.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students correctly identify and label the subatomic particles across at least three different visual representations of atoms.
materials: Printed worksheets with various atomic models
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes for explaining the different models, 25 minutes for labeling practice, 10 minutes for group review.
activities.task: Provide students with various printed diagrams of different atomic models (e.g., Bohr, Rutherford). Students must identify and label the subatomic particles in each different representation.

activities.differentiation: Provide larger print diagrams for students with visual impairments.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students score 1 point for correctly labeling the nucleus and 1 point for correctly placing protons/neutrons inside and electrons outside.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes for distributing papers and instructions, 30 minutes for independent work, 5 minutes for collection.
activities.task: Students complete a blank diagram of an atom under test conditions, labeling the nucleus, protons, neutrons, and electrons without using notes.

activities.differentiation: Allow verbal description for students unable to draw quickly.
activities.mastery_criterion: Students produce a recognizable sketch with all four key terms correctly placed.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes for distribution, 10 minutes for drawing, 5 minutes for holding up boards and teacher feedback.
activities.safety: Ensure adequate ventilation when using dry erase markers.

activities.differentiation: Provide a step-by-step guide on how to calculate neutrons.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly determines the number of subatomic particles for at least 4 out of 5 given elements.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes for instructions, 20 minutes for practice, 10 minutes for review.
activities.task: Students practice identifying the number of protons, neutrons, and electrons for various elements using their atomic numbers.

activities.differentiation: Provide a word bank for the names of the models.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly matches all three models and provides an accurate basic description for each.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes for instructions, 20 minutes for independent work, 5 minutes for collection.
activities.task: Students match the names of Döbereiner, Chancourtois, and Newlands with their respective classification models (triads, helix, octaves) and write a one-sentence description of each.

activities.differentiation: Include a visual reminder that atomic number equals proton count in a neutral atom.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly identifies the number of protons and electrons for all three elements.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes for instructions, 20 minutes for independent work, 5 minutes for collection.
activities.task: Given the atomic numbers of three elements, students state the number of protons and electrons for each neutral atom.

activities.differentiation: Provide a visual number line to help students calculate the net charge.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly identifies the ion type and charge for at least 4 out of 5 scenarios.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes for instructions, 20 minutes for practice, 10 minutes for peer review.
activities.task: Students are given a list of scenarios where atoms gain or lose specific numbers of electrons. They must determine if the resulting ion is a cation or an anion and write its overall charge.

activities.differentiation: Highlight the words 'gains' and 'loses' in the descriptions.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly classifies all three examples.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes for instructions, 20 minutes for independent work, 5 minutes for collection.
activities.task: Students read three short descriptions of atoms gaining or losing electrons and classify each as forming a cation or an anion.

activities.differentiation: Provide a sentence starter for the justification.
activities.mastery_criterion: Correctly compares the supplied records and limits the conclusion to the evidence shown.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes for instructions, 20 minutes for independent work, 5 minutes for collection.
activities.task: Compare two supplied, explicitly illustrative pairs of neutral-atom and positive-ion radius records. Identify the pattern in those pairs, then explain why those records alone do not prove an unrestricted rule for all comparisons.

activities.differentiation: Allow the use of a color-coded periodic table.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly assigns the oxidation number for all four elements.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes for instructions, 20 minutes for independent work, 5 minutes for collection.
activities.task: Given a list of four elements from groups 1, 2, 16, and 17, students determine the typical oxidation number for each.

activities.differentiation: Pair students strategically so they can support each other.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly identifies the larger atom and references the group or period trend.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes for setup, 20 minutes for the flashcard game, 5 minutes for wrap-up.
activities.task: Students participate in a quick flashcard game where they are shown pairs of elements and must quickly point to the one with the larger atomic radius, explaining the trend.

activities.differentiation: Use formulas with only two elements for students needing support.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly lists elements and atom counts for all three formulas.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes for instructions, 15 minutes for the activity, 10 minutes for class review.
activities.task: Students complete a 'do-now' mini-quiz on the board where they break down three common chemical formulas into their constituent elements and atom counts.

activities.differentiation: Provide pre-drawn tables for data collection. For advanced students, ask them to calculate the ratio of expansion between different pairs of dots.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student successfully creates a model showing proportional expansion between points and records accurate measurements.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes for introduction and safety, 20 minutes for the three stages of inflation and measurement, 15 minutes for data analysis, and 15 minutes for group discussion and conclusion writing.
activities.safety: Ensure students do not over-inflate balloons to prevent popping near faces. Students with latex allergies should use alternative silicone balloons or observe.
activities.task: Students work in pairs to draw dots on a deflated balloon, measure the distances between them with a flexible tape, inflate the balloon halfway, measure again, and then inflate fully and measure a final time. They record the data in a table and write a conclusion about how the distance between all points increases simultaneously.

activities.differentiation: Provide graph paper with pre-labeled axes. Challenge fast finishers to predict the position of a hypothetical mark beyond the elastic band's current length.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student accurately graphs the positions showing that marks further away move a greater distance than marks closer to the origin.
materials: thick elastic bands with permanent marker dots
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes for setup and safety briefing, 25 minutes for stretching and recording data, 20 minutes for graphing and peer review.
activities.safety: Students must wear safety goggles to protect eyes in case the elastic band snaps or slips.
activities.task: Students use a large elastic band with evenly spaced marks to model expansion along a single line of sight between galaxies. One student holds the end while another stretches it along a meter stick. They record the positions of the marks at rest, at 50cm stretch, and at 100cm stretch, graphing the movement of each mark relative to the starting point.

activities.differentiation: Allow the use of a calculator for coordinate multiplication. Provide a partially started grid for students needing visual support.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly plots the new coordinates (doubling the distance from the origin) and states that all points moved away from each other.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes for instructions, 25 minutes for independent grid drawing and calculation, 10 minutes for writing the explanation.
activities.safety: Standard classroom safety applies. Ensure clear walkways during the assessment.
activities.task: Students are given a worksheet with a diagram of a grid representing space with galaxies at specific coordinates. They must draw a second grid showing the universe expanded by a factor of two, placing the galaxies at their new coordinates and writing a short explanation of the model.

activities.differentiation: Provide a reference chart showing the visible light spectrum with wavelengths labeled. Ask advanced students to explain what a blueshift would mean.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly identifies that a shift toward longer wavelengths indicates an object is moving away and justifies this using the wave model.
materials: printed spectrum charts showing normal and shifted absorption lines
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes for the physical spring model, 20 minutes for analyzing the spectrum charts, 25 minutes for writing the justification and class sharing.
activities.safety: Ensure students do not release the stretched spring toy abruptly to avoid pinching fingers or hitting others.
activities.task: Students use a coiled spring toy (slinky) to model light waves. They stretch the spring while moving one end away from a stationary observer to simulate how wavelengths lengthen (redshift). They then review three hypothetical star spectrum charts and justify which stars are moving away based on the shift of absorption lines toward the red end.

activities.differentiation: Highlight the specific absorption lines on the cards for easier comparison. Require advanced students to order the 'moving away' galaxies by speed based on the degree of shift.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student accurately sorts the galaxies and links the red shift to the stretching of wavelengths and the object moving away.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes for card distribution and instructions, 30 minutes for sorting and group discussion, 20 minutes for independent writing.
activities.task: Students are given a set of cards with data from different galaxies, including their observed spectral lines compared to laboratory standards. They must sort the galaxies into 'moving away', 'moving closer', or 'stationary', and write a paragraph justifying their sorting based on the stretching or compressing of the light waves.

activities.differentiation: Provide a sentence starter for the justification section. Do not reduce the requirement to explain the wavelength stretching.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student links the red shift to the stretching of wavelengths and the object moving away in a clear written response.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes for reading the scenario, 25 minutes for drafting the response, 10 minutes for review and editing.
activities.task: Students read a scenario about a newly discovered galaxy whose light spectrum is heavily shifted toward the red end. They must write a formal scientific response determining the direction of its movement relative to Earth and justifying their answer using the concept of wavelength stretching.

activities.differentiation: Allow verbal responses for students with writing difficulties, recorded by the teacher.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly identifies the stretched wave as redshift and explains it indicates movement away from the observer.
materials: projector or printed images of waves
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes to display the image and explain the prompt, 15 minutes for writing, 10 minutes for peer exchange and discussion.
activities.task: Students participate in a quick-write activity where they are shown a single image of a stretched wave and a compressed wave. They must identify which represents redshift and explain why this means a galaxy is moving away from Earth.

activities.differentiation: Provide a glossary of terms (wavelength, spectrum, redshift) for reference.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly identifies false statements and rewrites them to accurately reflect that redshift means wavelengths are stretching as objects move away.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes to complete the quiz, 15 minutes to review answers as a class and correct misconceptions.
activities.task: Students are given a true/false quiz with statements about light waves and galaxy movement. For every false statement, they must rewrite it to make it true, specifically focusing on the relationship between redshift and expansion.

activities.differentiation: Provide printed labels with definitions for students to match to their clay models. Challenge advanced students to write the relative size of each stage.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly orders and models the stages from dust particles to a full planet.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes for introduction, 30 minutes for building the clay models sequentially, 20 minutes for labeling and gallery walk.
activities.safety: Ensure students wash hands after using clay. Do not allow tasting or throwing of clay.
activities.task: Students use different sizes of modeling clay to represent the stages of accretion. They start with tiny specks (dust), combine them into small balls (chondrules), then larger lumps (meteoroids/asteroids), and finally a large sphere (planet). They label each stage on a large piece of paper.

activities.differentiation: Number the backs of the cards for self-checking for students who struggle. Require advanced students to add transitional arrows explaining the physical process (gravity/collisions).
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly orders the stages from dust particles to a full planet on their timeline.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes for the sorting activity, 30 minutes for creating the timeline poster, 15 minutes for presenting posters to the class.
activities.task: Students work in small groups with a set of 20 cards containing images and descriptions of accretion stages. They must race to arrange them in the correct chronological order of formation, then create a timeline poster gluing the cards in sequence.

activities.differentiation: Provide a word bank with the terms. Do not provide the order.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly orders the stages from dust particles to a full planet and matches them to their descriptions.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes for instructions, 25 minutes for independent completion, 10 minutes for collection and quiet reading.
activities.task: Students complete a matching and sequencing worksheet where they must draw lines connecting the terms (dust, chondrules, meteoroids, asteroids, planetesimals, planets) to their definitions, and then write them in a numbered list from smallest/earliest to largest/latest.

activities.differentiation: Highlight key characteristics in the profiles for easier reading. Ask advanced students to identify which stage our Sun is currently in.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly identifies nebulae, main sequence stars, red giants, and white dwarfs based on their characteristics.
materials: reference texts on star life cycles
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes for reading the reference text, 30 minutes for analyzing and categorizing the profiles, 15 minutes for class review and correction.
activities.task: Students are given a set of 'stellar profile' folders containing characteristics (temperature, size, composition) of different star stages. They work in groups to categorize the profiles into nebula, main sequence, red giant, and white dwarf, using a reference text to verify their classifications.

activities.differentiation: Provide fewer cards per round for students who get overwhelmed. Require advanced students to write two facts per stage.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly matches at least 3 out of 4 stages to their descriptions and visuals.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 20 minutes for the matching game, 25 minutes for gluing and writing facts, 15 minutes for peer review.
activities.task: Students play a matching game where they must pair a card with a visual representation of a star stage to a card with its text description. Once all pairs are found, they glue them into their notebooks and write one additional fact for each stage.

activities.differentiation: Provide a word bank for students with IEPs requiring memory support. The cognitive demand of matching remains.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly identifies nebulae, main sequence stars, red giants, and white dwarfs from descriptions.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 5 minutes for instructions, 30 minutes for quiz completion, 10 minutes for collection.
activities.task: Students complete a written quiz where they are given four descriptions of stellar characteristics and must write the correct stage name next to each description without a word bank.

activities.differentiation: Provide a simplified flowchart with fewer intermediate steps. Ask advanced students to explain why mass dictates the core temperature and fusion rate.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student deduces that high-mass stars become supernovae/black holes while low-mass stars become white dwarfs, referencing mass as the determining factor.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 15 minutes for flowchart analysis, 25 minutes for tracing the case studies, 20 minutes for writing the justification.
activities.task: Students analyze a flowchart showing the life cycles of stars based on initial mass. They are given two case studies: Star A (0.8 solar masses) and Star B (25 solar masses). They must trace the path of each star on the flowchart and write a justification for their final evolutionary stages based on the mass data.

activities.differentiation: Provide the specific mass threshold (e.g., 8 solar masses) explicitly on the worksheet. Challenge advanced students to research and include neutron stars in their predictions.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly categorizes the stars based on mass and articulates that high mass leads to supernovae and low mass to white dwarfs.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes for setup, 30 minutes for categorizing the ten stars, 20 minutes for writing the summary paragraph.
activities.task: Students are given a list of ten hypothetical stars with their masses listed in solar masses. They must create a T-chart predicting whether each star will end as a white dwarf or undergo a supernova, and write a summary paragraph explaining the rule they used to make their predictions.

activities.differentiation: Allow students to draw a diagram to accompany and support their written explanation.
activities.mastery_criterion: Student correctly aligns mass with the final stage and references mass as the determining factor in their essay.
activities.rationale_for_minutes: 10 minutes for reading the prompt, 35 minutes for writing the essay.
